# ASSUMPTIONS.md

Every decision below goes beyond what EXPLORATION.md (EXP) observed directly. Each one has a status:
**OPEN** = needs kai's answer before the phase it affects · **DEFAULT** = I'll proceed with this unless kai objects · **CONFIRMED** = kai agreed.

## Where things stand after Phase 13 (2026-10-04)

94 numbered decisions (A-01 to A-99; numbers freed by merged items were not reused). 5 are CONFIRMED by kai (A-03, A-04, A-31, A-39, A-40), most are DEFAULT (applied as written, open to objection), 13 are marked ASSUMED where a formula or behaviour had to be read from the reference's screens (A-83, A-84, A-85, A-88, A-89, A-91, A-92, A-93, A-94, A-95, A-96, A-97, A-98), and these remain **OPEN** for kai:

- **Money and rules:** A-09 (which admin actions need CEO approval), A-10 (monthly charge and pro-rating), A-12 (salary methods), A-08 (membership transitions).
- **Permissions:** A-05 (the default permission matrix), A-34 (seeded matrix), A-44 (nobody grants more than they hold).
- **Schedule and courses:** A-50 (even days = Tue/Thu/Sat, odd = Mon/Wed/Fri), A-18 / A-42 (course-form step 2), A-16 (DTM levels).
- **Tests and coins:** A-19 / A-81 (minimal test model, "USUL" column), A-79 (what awards "Uy vazifasi" coins).
- **Integrations:** A-20 (providers), A-86 (which PBX), A-87 (which FaceID terminal).
- **Scope:** A-02 (vendor widgets left out), A-06 (student app), A-07 (parent portal).

An OPEN item changes nothing until answered; the DEFAULT next to it is what the code does today.

## Where things stand now (2026-11-12, after PR #111)

Everything built after Phase 13 is a numbered row from A-100 onwards, one row per item, in the order it was built; the newest rows are at the end of the last table. In short:

- **A-100 to A-108:** video lessons, the student's personal page, homework, Telegram for students and parents, materials and recordings with their retention, online payments (Payme and Click) and several organisations on one server.
- **A-109 to A-111:** the migration kit for a centre moving to Kampus: opening balances, billing start dates and catalogue imports.
- **A-112 to A-149:** round 2: debt collection, the teacher's Today screen, a centre's own address, the timetable with clash checks, weekly parent reports, referrals, cashier day close, instalments, absence and lead follow-up, announcements, trial lessons, the forecast, monitoring, the shared Telegram bot, dark theme, syllabus, waiting list, QR attendance, certificates, the SOFF CRM importer, the site-owner console, the lead inbox and the assistant.
- **A-150 to A-178:** online lessons round 3: student and parent sign-in with Telegram, attendance from calls, polls, whiteboard, breakout rooms, self-study content and exercises, gradebook, badges, class stream, vocabulary trainer, 1:1 self-booking, no-shows, ratings, group chat, lesson summaries, the installable student app, object storage, streaming copies, web push, time zones and lesson packages.
- **A-179:** how Telegram login is set up in BotFather today, and the shared bot decision.
- **A-180:** staff sign in with Telegram too, and a centre can switch to Telegram only (the switch was retired by A-196).
- **A-181:** the site owner can switch every centre on the server to Telegram only at once (retired by A-196).
- **A-182:** video lessons on tablets: the share button explains where the browser cannot share a screen and offers the whiteboard, the materials or the back camera; touch-size controls.
- **A-183, A-184:** show a material to everyone in a video lesson (PDF pages the teacher turns, pictures, video and audio in step, pen over a page) on phones, tablets and computers; zoom, a layout for phones held sideways, screen share with the tab's sound in Chrome and Edge, and a fix for files that did not play in the student app.
- **A-185:** the AI assistant answers only about the centre's work in Kampus and teaching questions, and declines other topics.
- **A-186, A-187:** found by teaching a test lesson on the live site: “today's lesson” follows the Tashkent day, and smaller repairs to homework, the student page, the video card and labels.
- **A-188:** every picture of the in-app manual retaken and 18 added (video lesson, checking queue, lesson packages, Telegram sign-in, student tabs), and `docs/DEMO-GUIDE.md`, a demo script that uses the same pictures.
- **A-189:** a whole centre copied from SOFF CRM by a script, dry run first: archived students, real join and leave dates, balances, payment history, attendance, leads, finance and exams, safe to run again.
- **A-190:** a daily summary for whoever opens Kampus: the director gets the whole centre, a branch manager the branch, a teacher their own groups; Kampus counts the figures, the AI writes only the conclusion, kept per person and day.
- **A-191:** the assistant floats over every staff page as a round button with a panel (Summary and Ask), and teachers may use it for their own groups.
- **A-192:** a modern look with motion: pages lift away and settle, a pressed name travels to the heading of its page, the figures on Home roll in as counters, lists and cards arrive in sequence, the sign-in page is a tiled wall that lights under the pointer, light and dark open in a circle; all of it off when the device asks for less motion. The header now fits a phone screen.
- **A-193:** a group's days can each have their own time (Monday 20:30, Friday 16:30); changing the days or times of a running group keeps the lessons already behind it and starts the new times today; a centre can let teachers change the times of their own groups; the students hear of it on Telegram.
- **A-194:** a short teacher view and a switch at the top of the page: someone who teaches and also holds another role (Teacher and Branch manager) picks **Teacher** to see only their next lesson with the video button, the day's lessons, homework to check and their own groups and students, and the other side for everything; the choice is kept on the account. Every teacher gets the short menu and the new top of Today.
- **A-195:** a teacher copies the lesson link from inside the video lesson: one button in the bar at the bottom (also under **People**), whether or not the screen is shared; the link is one address for the whole group, the same for every lesson, and whoever opens it signs in first and only students of that group get in.
- **A-196:** one way to sign in for everyone, staff, students and parents: phone number and password, and the first time a six-digit code that the Kampus bot sends to the person's Telegram chat (they share their number with the bot once). After the first sign-in the person chooses a password. Someone whose phone the centre does not have goes on a waiting list, and a teacher or manager lets them in under **Sign-in requests**. Both sign-in pages explain the Telegram steps. The **Telegram only** switches of A-180 and A-181 are retired.
- **A-197:** how-to videos: one short video per feature (23 of them, from signing in to the AI assistant), each in English, Russian and Uzbek with the caption of every step under the picture and, on request, read aloud by an Azure voice, recorded by a script from the demo seed (`npm run help:videos`); the videos are files outside the app.
- **A-198:** small page faults found while reviewing the videos: names no longer overprinted in the attendance and grades tables, the close-the-day window fits its table, the leads funnel names its stages beside the bars, Uzbek dates in the video lesson panel and the server status, payroll job titles in the reader's language, two internal notes removed from page descriptions; and from the second look: receipts print the right day on a server that is not on UTC and name the month a payment is for, forms opened after midnight start on today's date, a student's invite code no longer changes after the card is first opened, the payment history, exams and cash-desk tables fit the page, rolling figures sit on the line with their minus and currency, and the home page has no untranslated "NEW" badge.
- **A-199:** the how-to videos play inside Kampus: each Help topic that has a video shows it above its picture, **How-to videos** on the Help home lists them all, and the sign-in pages offer the one about signing in. The files are served by Kampus's own server from a folder beside the app (kai chose "Kampus server only", nothing on YouTube); a video that is not in the folder is not shown.
- **A-200:** screen sharing made dependable: a share that does not start says why (the computer refused, the window could not be captured) with **Try again**, instead of a button that does nothing; a shared screen takes the stage from the whiteboard, a shown file, a spotlight and an earlier pin; big screens go out at Full HD at most with a budget of their own, smaller as the room grows; the lesson's own tab is not offered and the computer's sound is shared only where voices do not come back as an echo; every failure leaves one line in the server log.
- **A-201:** a mini window (picture-in-picture) as in Google Meet: in Chrome and Edge on a computer the lesson's people stay in a small window on top when the person switches tabs, with microphone, camera, back and leave buttons; it opens by itself on a tab switch and closes on the way back, and a button in the bar opens it by hand. Safari on a computer floats one picture; Firefox, phones and tablets have none.
- **A-202:** the server can move to a new address (kampus.center instead of the sslip.io name): pages opened under the old name lead to the same page under the new one, and webhooks registered under the old name still arrive.
- **A-203:** the phone app signs in without cookies: the same sign-in calls answer the app with a session token, which it keeps in the phone's protected storage and sends with every call. An app session lasts 30 days from its last use (a browser's still 12 hours) and shows in **Devices** as "Kampus app". Nothing changes for browsers.
- **A-204:** from the app to the site without signing in twice: for a page the app does not have yet (the lesson room, the office's tables) the app asks for a link that works once, within a minute, and opens the page in the phone's browser already signed in.
- **A-205:** the Kampus app for phones and tablets, written in React Native (kai's choice), one project for Android, iOS and the web, in `mobile/`. First version: sign-in, the teacher's day on a phone and on an iPad (today's lessons, attendance, grades, topic, homework, the lesson room, groups, homework checking) and the student's and parent's home with their group's lessons, grades and payments. Not in the stores yet; the site stays as it is and will move to the app's code part by part.
- **A-206:** the build no longer packs the whole repository into the app's server image. The how-to videos are read from a folder named by a setting, and the bundler, unable to tell which folder that is, copied the project's source, tests, docs and `mobile/` into the server output and printed six warnings on every build since A-199. The six calls now carry the bundler's ignore hint; the server output went from 233 MB to 170 MB and the warnings are gone. Nothing changes on the site.
- **A-207:** the lesson room is inside the app: a teacher starts or joins the lesson, and a student joins it, with the phone's or tablet's own camera and microphone, without the browser. It is the same room as on the site (the same people, chat, hands, reactions, spotlight, focus, mute, end for everyone), so someone in the app and someone in a browser are in one lesson. Since A-208 to A-211 the app also has screen sharing from Android, the whiteboard, shown files, the teacher's polls and breakout rooms. Not in the app yet: sharing the screen of an iPhone or iPad, and recording.
- **A-208:** in the app on Android a teacher or a student shares the phone's or tablet's screen with the lesson (the phone asks first, every time), and a lesson keeps its microphone and camera while another app is in front: Android shows a "Lesson in progress" notice that leads back. Sharing the screen of an iPhone or iPad is not in the app yet.
- **A-209:** the whiteboard is in the app: the teacher opens it from **Lesson tools**, draws with a finger or a pen in five colours and three widths, erases, undoes and clears, and decides whether students may draw. It is the site's whiteboard: what is drawn in the app appears in a browser and the other way round.
- **A-210:** files shown to everyone are in the app. The teacher picks one of the lesson's or the group's materials under **Lesson tools → Show a file to everyone**; a PDF's pages turn for everyone, a picture or a page can be drawn on, a video or audio file plays in step with the teacher's player, a YouTube link plays in the lesson, and a link or an office file is a card with a button. A student in the app sees whatever a teacher shows from the app or from a computer.
- **A-211:** the teacher runs polls and breakout rooms from the app. **Lesson tools → Poll**: a question with two to six answers, live counts with the names behind each answer, **Close and show results**, **New poll**. **Lesson tools → Breakout rooms**: two to six rooms for 5 to 30 minutes or until closed, students dealt round the rooms in turn, a countdown, **Go there** to drop in on a room, move one student, a message to every room, and **Close the rooms and bring everyone back**. They are the site's polls and rooms, so students in a browser and in the app take part alike.
- **A-212:** a student or parent answers homework inside the app: the **Homework** page of a group lists every task with its state; an answer is text, a photo taken on the spot, a photo or a file from the phone (up to 20 MB), or for a speaking task a recording made in the app. The teacher's score, comment and voice reply show on the task. The task's file, the student's own file and the teacher's voice reply open inside the app (PDF, picture, video, audio); other kinds are handed to another app on the phone. Since A-213 the task's exercises, tests, the chat and materials are in the app too.
- **A-213:** a group's **Tests**, **Materials** and **Chat** are pages of the app, beside **Homework**, and a homework task's self-check exercises are done in the app. A test runs with the server's clock, asks before handing in and hands in by itself when the time is up. Materials are sorted under their lessons; a file or a lesson recording opens in the app, and a recording continues where the student stopped on any device. The chat is the group's one chat (site, app, Telegram). Still on the personal page: the course, news, the stream, the schedule with booking, and paying online.
- **A-214:** the teacher's side of a group is in the app. **Checking** opens a student's file inside the app and plays a spoken answer in place; the teacher can answer with a written comment, a reply recorded on the phone, or both, and returning an answer takes a second press. A group's screen has **Chat** (the group's one chat, with the unread number) and **Materials** (everything the students see, with who watched a recording), and a teacher adds to the materials from the phone: a photo taken on the spot, a photo or file from the phone, or a link, for the whole group or for a lesson. In a lesson, **Show a file to everyone** can take a photo or file from the phone into the lesson's materials first. The same pull request fixes what the first run on devices found (A-208 to A-210).
- **A-215:** more of the student's and parent's side is in the app, so the group's screen now lists eight pages. **Course** shows the topics with what the teacher opened (text, video, files, links, self-check exercises), the student's progress and the **Vocabulary trainer** (flashcards). **Stream** is the class stream with comments; **News** is the centre's notices with the unread number; **Results** is the grade part by part, badges, exams and tests taken. Under each past lesson the student rates it with one to five stars and may add a line. A file on a stream post now opens from the student's side (it did not before, on the site either). The schedule with booking and paying online still open the personal page.
- **A-216:** the rest of the student's and parent's personal page is in the app, so nothing on a group's screen opens the site any more. **Schedule** shows the weekly times and the next lessons; where the centre lets a one-to-one student arrange lessons, they move or cancel a lesson, pick a new time for a lesson that was taken off and book an extra one, from the teacher's free times when the teacher keeps booking hours. **Your time zone** sits on the same page. **Pay online** takes the amount and the month and opens Payme's or Click's page over the app, then shows when the money landed. **Telegram** connects the centre's bot and removes a connected chat. **Invite a friend** shows the code and shares the link through the phone's share sheet. **Results** lists certificates. Two small read-only calls were added on the server for the invite code and the certificates.
- **A-217:** a teacher's group in the app has four more pages: **Homework**, **Stream**, **Gradebook** and **Notes**. Homework lists every task with who answered, sets a task for a lesson or starts a named assignment with a link, a file or photo from the phone, a due day and the speaking mark, and checks waiting answers right under their task. An assignment with a rubric asks for the points of each criterion before it is accepted, in the group and on **Checking**. Stream writes to the group with a file, pins a post, closes its comments, answers and removes. Gradebook and Notes are read on the phone; a note is added by whoever may change the group. Editing a lesson's homework from the app or from **Today** on the site no longer drops its link, file or speaking mark.
- **A-218:** a teacher's group in the app has three more pages: **Syllabus**, **Tests** and **Coins**. Syllabus shows the course's topics with what was covered and what comes next, lets the teacher choose when the students get a topic's content (after the lesson, now, or from a day), and shows how far each student is. Coins lists the group by balance and gives coins to one student for one of the centre's reasons, with a comment. Tests lists the tests given to the group with how many handed them in and how well, and opens the results of this group's students; a test is still written on the site.
- **A-219:** the rest of a teacher's group is in the app: **Exams** (each exam with its day, room and examiner, and the scores of this group's students), **Knowledge analysis** (right answers by topic over the group's tests, for one subject or one test), **Comments** (notes about one student, read and written from the phone) and **History** (what was changed about the group, by whom and when). A group's screen shows its six daily pages and keeps the rest behind **More pages**. The history, on the site too, now names stream posts, topic openings and students' bookings instead of calling them "Edited" or showing a raw key.
- **A-220:** teachers have **Students** in the app, as a fifth place beside Today, Groups, Checking and More: the students of their groups by name, found by name or phone, and one student's page with a **Call** button for the student and each parent, the groups (each opens the group), **Progress** (grade, attendance, months, exams), **Test results** and **Comments and notes** with a new note written from the phone. A student in a group's list opens the same page.
- **A-221:** **Announcements** are in the app, from **More**: the notices the person may see, with where each went and how many read it, and a new one to one of their groups (title, text, **Also send by SMS**). **Delete** asks once more. A notice to a whole branch or the whole centre is still posted from the site.
- **A-222:** the teacher saves the **whiteboard** from the app's lesson room: one button on the board's tools, and the picture lies under the group's materials for that lesson, as from the site. Checked in a lesson in the app's web build; on a phone and a tablet it is still to be checked.
- **A-223:** **Share screen** is in the app on an iPhone and an iPad too: the button opens Apple's own "Screen Broadcast" sheet with Kampus chosen, and after **Start Broadcast** everyone sees the screen, also while another app is in front. Built and checked as far as a computer can; **never tried on a real iPhone or iPad yet**, because that needs Apple's developer account.
- **A-224:** The app has **glass and motion**: the navigation bar on a phone, the header of every screen, the save bar and the lesson room's buttons and sheet are panes the page shows through, as on an iPhone, on Android too; presses, lists, the chosen place and pushed screens move smoothly. Apple's own Liquid Glass on iOS 26 and later, a blur elsewhere, a solid surface where the device asks for one. **Seen only in a browser so far, not on a phone.**
- **A-225:** The **site has glass** too: the top bar, menus and lists that drop down, dialogs and the drawer on the right, the assistant's panel, and the bar along the bottom of a phone (now a rounded pane that floats, with a turquoise fill on the page you are on). Cards, tables and the lapis sidebar stay solid. A browser that cannot blur, and a device set to less transparency, get the solid surfaces as before.
- **A-226:** An upload is known by **what the file is, not by the name a device gives its type**: an iPhone sends a voice recording as `audio/x-m4a` whatever the app asks for, and the server refused it ("This file type is not accepted") for a student's spoken answer and a teacher's voice reply. The server now takes the other names devices use for the types it already accepts (m4a, mp3, wav, jpeg, zip), and a file that comes with no type at all goes by the ending of its name. No new kind of file is accepted.
- **A-227:** **Homework to do** on a student's home (site and app) lists **assignments that belong to no lesson** too (A-161): the list asked for the lesson's date and left them out, so a new essay showed only on the Homework page. An assignment is listed while its due date, or the day it was set when it has none, is within the last 21 days or ahead.
- **A-228:** **Glass and motion after the first look on the simulators** (iPhone, iPad, Android phone and tablet): on Android the page behind a pane has its own colour (a dark header came out grey) and the pane is thinner so the page shows through; going back to a tab no longer blinks and cards arrive sooner; an iPhone and iPad show the app's own reload sign under the header when a page is pulled down; the lesson's tools sheet is as tall as its buttons; the chat beside a lesson on a tablet and the sign-in on Android make room for the keyboard.
- **A-229:** **The app's sign-in screen: first sign-in, its video and the tiled wall**: under the sign-in form the app says that a new account is approved by the centre's staff, and offers a video "How to sign in for the first time" once the server has the one recorded in the app itself (the site's videos say there is nothing to install). The site's staff sign-in page carries the same title and line. On a tablet the lapis panel is the site's star-and-cross wall, and a touch on it runs rings of lit tiles, like a drop on water.
- **A-230:** **Every site feature in the app, part 1: the centre's home, the bell, search, the menu and "My salary"**: in the app the office starts at Home with the same twelve figures behind **Show numbers**, the setup checklist, the revenue forecast, the rooms of a weekday and the money of a year or a month; a bell and a search stand on top of it; **More** lists every page the person may open, in the app where the app has it and on the site (already signed in) where it does not yet; "My salary" is in the app. Teachers keep their four places. Details in the table below.
- **A-231:** **Every site feature in the app, part 2: students for the office**: in the app the students list takes the site's filters (payment status, status in the group, course, group, teacher, the archive), so a figure of the home page opens the list already narrowed; **Add student** is a form with the name, phone, day of birth, a group to join and a parent; a student's page has **Make a payment** (the site's Payment dialog) and a **Payments** part. Details in the table below.
- **A-232:** **Every site feature in the app, part 3: leads and the people to call**: the app has the leads board (one column at a time on a phone, side by side on a tablet), a lead's card with log a contact, book a trial, history, edit, into a group, onto the waiting list, another column, archive and delete; Calls today; the waiting list; the inbox of chats with replies through the bot; sign-in requests; and absences with their contact log. Boards, columns, sources, bulk actions and the Excel export stay on the site.
- **A-233:** **Every site feature in the app, part 4a: groups for the office and the timetable**: the Groups tab gives the office every group with the site's filters, a search and **New group**; the group form has the site's rules (one time for all days or a time per day, from which day new times count, a busy room or teacher named with "Save anyway"); a group's page shows what the group is and offers edit, change times, change teacher, support teachers, a day off (and taking one back), move to another branch, finish and archive; **Manage students** lists the group's students with balances and adds, moves, removes and activates them; a student's page has **Add to a group**; **Timetable** shows a room's or a teacher's week. Two read-only calls were added on the server for the app. Packages, discounts, the Excel files and SMS stay on the site.
- **A-234:** **Every site feature in the app, part 4b: teachers, courses, rooms and the Settings list**: **Teachers** in the More menu opens the two lists (teachers, support teachers) with a search and the archive, **New teacher**, and a teacher's page with how they are paid, three counts, their groups and their hours open for 1:1 booking; the form has no password field, because a first sign-in is with a code from Telegram. **Settings** lists the site's sections the person may open; **Courses** (with the syllabus and grade weights) and **Rooms** are in the app, the rest open on the site. A teacher finds their own 1:1 hours under More. Nothing new on the server for these pages. Fixed from the iPhone and iPad run: a payment type that stayed chosen after its list was gone, sheets that let bright buttons glow through, the keyboard coming back after a list, the tablet's clock on the dark rail, and the day's summary opening over a page asked for from the app.
- **A-235:** **Every site feature in the app, part 4c: exams**: **Exams** in the More menu opens the centre's exams as two lists, group exams and mock exams, with the site's filters (status, group, from, to) and **Add exam**. An exam opens its own page: what it is and when, **Edit**, **Finish** or **Reopen**, **Delete** while nobody is graded, and the grading sheet, where each student gets Present, a score and a comment, saved together. A mock exam also has its registrations: a search by name or phone registers a student until the seats are taken, and a row takes one off after a question. On a group's Exams page, whoever may add exams adds one for that group, and each exam opens its page. Nothing new on the server.
- **A-236:** **Every site feature in the app, part 5a: debts and the cash desk**: **Debtors** in the More menu (and Home's Debtors figure) opens who owes the centre money: the four figures on top, a search by name or phone, the site's filter (open and promised, need a call, closed, all) and an order (longest overdue, most owed, promise, last contact, name). A press on a debtor offers **Call and log the outcome**, **Log a contact**, **Send a Telegram reminder**, **History** and the student's page; the phone numbers dial. **Cash desk** opens the day closes of a month or a year with their totals, **Close the day** for whoever takes payments (the day's figures by payment type, the expected cash, the counted cash and the difference) and **Accept** for the manager the money is handed to. **Print** opens the sheet on the site. Nothing new on the server.
- **A-237:** **Every site feature in the app, part 5b: finance and payroll**: **Finance** in the More menu opens the site's Finance page: the key figures of a year or a month, income by payment type, the year by months, the month's plan, expenses and income by category with **Category** to add one, bonuses, fines and the cash desk, and the payroll months. Every card opens its list (advances, marketing, bonuses, fines, investments, a category), where entries are added, changed and deleted with the site's one form. A payroll month shows each salary with what it is made of, **Approve** on a line, **Recalculate**, **Save draft** and **Save**; its Excel file opens on the site. One new read-only call on the server adds up the sums written on the page's cards.
- **A-238:** **Every site feature in the app, part 5c: reports**: **Reports** in the More menu opens the site's list of reports, and seven of the ten are in the app: Payments, Student payments, Left students, Lead statements, Referral programme, Students and Center statistics, each with the site's filters, figures, charts and rows. Graduates, Staff attendance and Coins open on the site until the next part. A report's Excel file opens the same report on the site. In Left students, **Set up reasons** adds, switches off and removes the reasons offered when a student leaves. One new read-only call on the server gives that report's filters their courses, teachers and groups. A fix on the site came with it: switching a "Transfer" reason off or on no longer turns it into a "Leaving" reason.
- **A-239:** **Every site feature in the app, part 5d: the last three reports**: Graduates, Staff attendance and Coins are in the app, so all ten reports now open there. **Graduates** shows the month's figures and each graduate; someone who may change students records the result (IELTS, CEFR, university, work), issues a certificate and revokes one. **Staff attendance** has the day's figures and the site's five tabs (daily, weekly, monthly, statistics, work schedules); someone who may change staff corrects a check-in or check-out and sets a person's working week. **Coins** has the rating with each student's history, the marketplace (products with a picture, categories) and the purchase requests, which someone who manages coins approves or rejects. Nothing changes on the server.
- **A-240:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6a: the rest of a student's page for the office**. A student's page in the app now has **SMS** (what was sent, and Send SMS with templates and the count of characters), **Calls** (the recorded calls and a call through the centre's telephony) and **History** for the office, next to groups, progress, tests, comments and payments. The **Parents** card adds and removes a parent and texts all of them. The **Family** card links a brother or sister, sets the family's name and discount, takes the student out of the family and opens the **Parents' page** link to share, text or replace. **Kampus app sign-in** lists the Telegram accounts that open the student and signs one out or removes it. The card itself adds and removes extra information, opens the badge to print on the site, and puts the student on the blacklist or takes them off it. Each of them asks for the same right as on the site. Nothing changes on the server.
- **A-241:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6b: a student's group cards and money**. For the office, each group on a student's page in the app is now the site's card: the balance, the status, the dates, the price, a discount, a split fee and the **lesson calendar** of a month with what each lesson was (paid, debt, excused, absent, upcoming). The three dots on a card change the status, take a payment into that group, **split the month's fee** into two or three parts, move the student to another group, return them to leads or remove them from the group. Groups the student has left stay behind **Show archived groups**. The **Payments** section gains **Refund**, **Adjust balance**, one group's payments, the receipt (opens on the site to print), the fiscal receipt's state with **Retry**, the list of opening balances and corrections, and the payments carried over from the old system. Each asks for the same right as on the site. The server gains one read-only call, `GET /api/v1/students/:id/payment-history`; until the server is updated the app shows everything except the old system's payments.
- **A-242:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 1: five settings pages**. Settings in the app now opens **Days off**, **Schools**, **SMS templates**, **Receipt settings** and **Coin settings** as screens of its own, next to Courses and Rooms. Days off: the dates with no lessons at a branch, add (telling that day's students and parents unless switched off), change, delete. Schools: add, rename, delete. SMS templates: the texts under their categories, a category or a template added, a template changed or deleted, an empty category deleted, the provider's templates copied in. Receipt: the address, phone, the parts on the receipt, the logo's place and the words at the foot, with a sample receipt that follows each choice. Coins: the switch for automatic coins, how many each event gives, and the reasons for coins given by hand. The other settings still open on the site. Nothing changes on the server.
- **A-243:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 2: General settings**. Settings in the app now opens **General settings** as a screen of its own, in five tabs. **Center settings**: the centre's name, working hours and schedule step, when debt reminders and the absence rules fire, the referral bonus, how late a 1:1 student may move a lesson, the public page, and the sixteen yes-or-no rules; Save wakes once something differs. **Branches**: add, rename, switch off after a question, switch back on. **Payment methods**: add, change (name, order, active, cash), delete. **Grading systems**: a name, the rounding and the levels with their scores, changed whole, deleted after a question that says how many courses use it. **Auto SMS settings**: each event with whether it sends and its text; a tap opens the switch, the text and that event's words in braces. Nothing changes on the server.
- **A-244:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 3: Staff and Roles**. Settings in the app now opens **Staff** and **Roles**. Staff: everyone who signs in, with a search, a chip per role with how many hold it, and the archive; a new staff member (name, phone, dates, branches, at least one role, how they are paid); a press on a person to change their card, switch the Telegram sign-in code, sign them out everywhere or archive them. Nobody changes their own roles or archives themselves, and no password is typed for anyone in the app. Roles: each role with how many permissions and people it has; a new role or a change to one, with a tick per permission under its module, greyed where the person does not hold it themselves; delete for the centre's own roles. Excel export and import of staff stay on the site. Nothing changes on the server.
- **A-245:** **On an iPhone or iPad a sheet opened from another sheet waits until that one has left.** A form opened from a menu (a group's **Split the month's fee** and **Return to leads**, a course's **Syllabus** and **Edit course**) never appeared on an iPhone or iPad: the menu closed and nothing followed. iOS shows one window over a screen at a time and refused the second while the first was still sliding away. Now the menu slides away first and the form comes right after it, about a fifth of a second later. Android was not affected and behaves as before. Found by the simulator run of 24 November.
- **A-246:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 4a: the logs, calls and payments**. Settings in the app now opens **Login log**, **Action log**, **Sent SMS**, **Calls** and **Payments**: the site's five lists to read, newest first, thirty rows at a time with **Show more**. Each has the site's filters: a search, From and To, and its own choices (outcome; type and staff member; status and sender; direction and status; payment method and cashier). The payments list shows the sum of everything the filters let through; a student's name opens their page; the receipt and the Excel file open on the site. One small read-only call is new on the server (the staff to choose from in the action log and the SMS log); until the server is updated those two lists work without that choice. 15 of the 22 Settings sections are in the app.
- **A-247:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 4b: Bot notifications and Forms**. Settings in the app now opens **Bot notifications** (the staff the Telegram bot writes to: add a person with their special ID and branches, remove one after a question) and **Forms** (the public lead forms: add, change and delete one, with the column its leads land in, the source and a note). The site copies a form's link on a click; a phone has no such click, so each form has **Share link**, which hands the address to the phone's share sheet, and **Open the form**, which shows it in the browser. Nothing changes on the server. 17 of the 22 Settings sections are in the app.
- **A-248:** **Small repairs in the app from the simulator run of 24 November.** Adding a student to a group they are in, or once left, now says "This student is already in the group." under the student, in the group's own sheet, on a student's page and when moving between groups (the server refused it before too, but the app showed nothing or "This value is already in use."). For the office on a phone, a group's page starts with **Manage students** and what the group is, before the month of lessons; a teacher still meets the lessons first, and a tablet is unchanged. English now says "1 recipient", "1 student activated" and "1 membership activated", on the site too. Not changed: a student who left a group cannot be added to the same group again, on the site either (a lead who comes back is taken back into the old place); the timetable is a typical week on the site too; the site does not warn about a second lead with the same phone either.
- **A-249:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 5a: Integrations, AmoCRM and FaceID**. - **A-250:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 5b: Tests and the question bank**. Once results are in, a test's questions are locked, as on the site. Twenty-one of the 22 settings sections are in the app; only the import from the old CRM is left. **One fault on the site is fixed with it:** **Edit** in the list of tests opened the form without the test's questions, so saving took a draft's questions away, and a test with results could not be saved at all. Edit now loads the whole test first.
- **A-251:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 5c: the import from the old CRM**. With this every one of the 22 settings sections is in the app; only the site owner's Organisations page stays on the site. Two small things change on the site with it: a row that is left out now says why in words (**Full name: Required.** where it said `fullName: validation.required`), and a preview made for one branch no longer lets the file into another branch without a new preview.
- **A-252:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6d, step 1: the manual with its videos**. The app's menu now ends with **Help**, as the site's side menu does: the same articles in the same order with the same words, pictures and how-to videos as the site's Help pages, in the app's language. The search is the site's own, so both find the same sections, and a result opens the article at its section. A picture opens large enough to read with a press, a video is fetched only when it is pressed, and **Open the page** goes to that page in the app. The pictures and films show the site, which the app follows page by page. Needs the server update: the server answers the manual to the app through two new read-only calls.
- **A-253:** **Every site feature in the app, part 6d, step 2: the assistant**. The app now has the site's assistant as one screen with two tabs. **Summary** shows the figures of yesterday, today or the last seven days with a conclusion, as the site's floating assistant does; a figure opens the page it counts inside the app. **Ask** is the conversation, with the same first questions for the office and for teachers. The sparkle button on Home opens the summary and carries a dot until today's summary has been looked at; the app does not open it by itself. Everyone the site shows the assistant to has it in the menu. Needs the server update: one new read-only call tells the app who is asking and whether the centre has a key.
- **A-254:** **Every site feature in the app, leftovers, step 1: a group's discounts and lesson packages**. A group that sells lessons by the package also has **Packages**: the packages on offer (add, change, stop selling), how many lessons every student has bought, used and has left, **Sell a package** (a payment and the lessons at once), and the packages sold. - **A-255:** **Every site feature in the app, leftovers, step 2: a person's photo**. - **A-256:** **Every site feature in the app, leftovers, step 3: Excel files on the phone**. The file is the list as it is filtered in the app. An iPhone or iPad shows it full screen with the system's own button to save it or send it on; an Android phone puts it in Downloads and opens it. A column has its own three dots (beside its name on a tablet, beside **Add lead** on a phone): **Rename column** and **Delete**. The server keeps a board that still has leads, a column that still has leads and a board's last column, and the app says which in words. Where a centre has no board yet, **New board** is on the empty page. **Sources** is the site's report: each source with its leads and how many became students in the chosen days, and sources can be added, renamed, switched off and deleted there. Archiving and restoring ask first; afterwards a line says how many were done and how many skipped, and the ticks are cleared. - **A-260:** **Every site feature in the app, leftovers, step 7: several students at once, an SMS to the whole list, and Activate**. With students ticked a bar shows above the list, as on the site: **Add to group**, **Give a discount**, **Send SMS**, **Excel (selected)**, **Archive** (in the archive: **Restore**) and **Clear**, each for whoever may do it. Afterwards a line says how many were done and how many skipped. Under the list, beside **Excel**, are the site's two other buttons: **Send SMS** writes one message to everyone the search and the filters show, and **Activate** makes every new and trial student among those listed active today, after a question. No server update is needed.

The person's card at the top of **More** opens **My account**, the site's page of that name: the password (when it was last changed, and a button to change it), **Ask for a code by Telegram** at sign-in, and the devices the person is signed in on, with **Sign out** on each other device and **Sign out everywhere else**. The sweep itself compared every call the server offers with the calls the app makes; this is the first of what it found. No server update is needed.
- **A-262:** **Every site feature in the app, the last sweep, step 2: a group's lessons**. On a group's page the office adds an **Extra lesson** (a day and its hours, starting from the group's usual hours), and **More** has **Offer seats to the waiting list** with the free seats and who is next in line. **Students' links** (among the group's pages and on a lesson's room card) lists each student's own link to the video lessons: share one or all, make a new link for one student after a question, and text everybody theirs. A lesson has the rest of the site's lesson window: the topic from the course plan, a note for the students, a link, and the students' ratings; the month shows a lesson's average rating and names an extra lesson. No server update is needed.
- **A-263:** **Every site feature in the app, the last sweep, step 3: a topic's content, words and exercises**. Every topic of a group's plan has a **Content** button. Its page holds what the students read, watch and download for the topic (text, a video, a file, a link), put in order and saved as a whole list; the topic's **self-check exercises** of the site's six kinds, each with how the students did; and the **words for the trainer**, one to a line. A homework has its exercises too, on a page of their own. The office or a teacher of the course changes them, everybody else reads. No server update is needed.
- **A-264:** **Every site feature in the app, the last sweep, step 4: attendance by badge, and a student's badges**. **Scan badges** on Today (for the door) and on a lesson's attendance opens a screen where the phone's or tablet's camera reads a student's badge and marks the student present; a hand scanner or the keyboard works too, and every badge gets a line saying what came of it. A student's page shows, with the progress, the badges the student earned and the ones still to earn. The app gains a camera module, so this needs a new build of the app; no server update is needed.
- **A-265:** **Every site feature in the app, the last sweep, step 5: the rest of the student form, and the school filter**. **Add student** in the app now has everything the site's form has: the password of the student's own sign-in, where they came from, who brought them, the time zone of a student abroad, how they join the group (new, trial, active), their own price and the day charging starts, and the school. **Edit student** also changes boy or girl, the time zone and the school. The students' filters gain **School**. This ends the sweep: what is left on the site only is listed in MOBILE-APPS. No server update is needed.
- **A-266:** **Repairs from the simulator run of the finished app (run 17)**. Main ba81f96 was built with the camera module and gone through on an iPhone 17 and an iPad Air simulator against the local server; the fault of run 16 (a form opened from a menu never appeared) is gone. The repairs were then looked at on the same simulators before they were merged. Found and repaired: a badge code sent with Enter, as a hand scanner sends it, lost its last letter and read "Not a badge"; every time zone read "(GMT)" with no offset; on Leads the Owner filter was squashed to a dot beside **Archive**; on a tablet's Today a lesson's room was cut to one letter beside **Extra**; "1 items"; the sentence on More that still named payments, leads, reports and settings as site-only; a reason field labelled with the words of the choice above it. On a phone the newest badge is now also said above the code field, where the keyboard does not cover it. Two things the run met are rules of the site, the same there and in the app, and are OPEN for kai: money and status dates follow the server's day, so between midnight and 05:00 Tashkent a discount or an activation carries yesterday's date (A-186 kept it so), and a student who joins in the middle of a month is listed on that month's earlier lessons as not marked.
- **A-267:** **A privacy policy, and deleting one's own account** (for Google Play and the App Store). Both stores ask for a public privacy policy and, where a person can open an account in the app, for a way to delete it in the app and on a web address. The site gets two public pages in three languages, `/privacy` and `/delete-account`. A student opens their own sign-in with a Telegram code, so a student deletes it themselves, at once: **Delete my account** on the student's home (site and app) removes the sign-in, its Telegram link and its codes; the centre's record of the student stays. A staff account is the centre's, so staff **ask**: **Delete my account** on My account marks the request and tells everyone who may archive staff; the person can take it back. OPEN (kai): the e-mail address the public may write to (`LEGAL_CONTACT_EMAIL`); the policy's text is Claude's draft and should be read before the store page goes out.
- **A-268:** **Ready for Google Play**. The store takes an app bundle signed with the app's own upload key, built for Android 16 with libraries that work on 16 KB memory pages. A build plugin signs the release with the upload key when the build is given one; the **Google Play bundle** workflow builds the `.aab` from kai's key in the repository's secrets and checks its signature and page sizes. kai makes the key on the Mac with one script; Claude never sees it or its password. The store page's texts in three languages, the icon, the banner and 26 screenshots are ready. What kai enters in Play Console, with the answers for its forms, is in docs/PLAY-STORE.md. On the way: the inline tick box on a phone lost its label's last letter in Uzbek ("Arxi").

Rule since 2026-11-10 (kai): every change updates the docs in the same piece of work. That means a row here, the in-app help in uz, ru and en when a page or a setup step changes, and DEPLOY.md when the server routine changes.

| A-44  | **Nobody grants more than they hold.** A user may only assign roles (and build custom roles from permissions) whose permissions are a subset of their own, may not edit a colleague who holds a role they could not grant (so an admin cannot reset the CEO's password), and may not change their own roles or archive themselves. With the default matrix this means an admin can manage teachers, support teachers, parents and "other" staff, while cashiers, marketers and watchers (who hold finance permissions) need a branch manager or the CEO. | A-59  | **Charging follows the membership's activation.** A membership is charged from the day it became ACTIVE (`activatedAt`, or the join date when it was created ACTIVE): one charge per course month, pro-rated by the lessons that fall inside the membership window in that month (joined/activated ≤ lesson date < left, and < frozen). NEW and TRIAL members are not charged; FROZEN stops further charging until reactivation. Past months are frozen as charged; the current month is recomputed on every read, so adding or removing a lesson changes the current charge only. Balance = payments + bonus − refunds − charges, per membership and summed per student. The next payment date is the first unpaid month when in debt, otherwise the next uncharged month up to the course end; the suggested amount is the debt, or one monthly price when nothing is owed. | A-75  | **Payroll is computed per month on first open of `/finance/salary-detail/:month`** and recomputed with "Qayta hisoblash". Per staff member: Doimiy = fixed salary when the salary method is Oylik; Foiz = group share % × course price × students of that group in the month (members not NEW/TRIAL whose window overlaps the month); Dars = per-lesson share × lessons held in the month (only lessons with marked attendance when "faqat kelgan darslar" is on; group day-offs added when "dam berilganida" is on); O'quvchi = per-student share × students; Bonus, Jarima (sum and count) and Avans from the ledger for the month; Maosh = fixed + percent + lessons + students + bonus − fines − advances. Group shares come from the group's teacher rows (EXP §5); support teachers are not paid in v1. "Tasdiqlash" approves one row and an approved row survives recalculation; "Vaqtincha saqlash" and "Saqlash" set the run status. The Excel export arrived with Phase 12. | A-100 | **Video lessons ("Online dars", added after v1 at kai's request 2026-10-05) are browser-to-browser WebRTC calls with Kampus as the only server.** Each browser sends its camera and microphone to every other one (full mesh); Kampus stores the room, who is in it and relays offers, answers and ICE candidates through a `VideoSignal` table that each browser polls about once a second, so no media server, vendor account or payment is needed. Address discovery uses public STUN servers (Google, Cloudflare); a TURN relay (static username/password, or coturn's shared secret for short-lived passwords) can be added under Settings → Integrations → Video lessons for networks that block direct calls. The call is tied to a group and, when one exists, to today's lesson; starting and ending it needs `groups.attendance.mark` in the group's scope (teachers of the group, admins, managers), anyone with `groups.view` may sit in as a guest, so no new permission codes were added. Students have no accounts (A-06): each current membership (NEW, TRIAL, ACTIVE) gets a personal link `/class/<token>` that works for every lesson of that group, can be copied, sent by SMS or replaced. One LIVE room per group; a room nobody has been in for 15 minutes is closed on the next look, and every call ends by itself 150 minutes after it started (kai, 2026-10-06); the same person joining again closes their earlier tab. The default limit is 12 people per call (mesh upload grows with each participant; bitrates step down as the room grows). The group card shows which students joined the last call and for how long; attendance is still marked by hand. | A-103 | **Telegram for students and parents (added 2026-10-06 at kai's request) rides on the staff bot.** Settings → Integrations → Telegram gains the bot's username; with it set, the student's page (A-101) shows "Connect Telegram", a `t.me/<bot>?start=<code>` link with a per-student code, and the webhook links the chat on `/start <code>` (`/stop` unlinks; the portal can also remove a chat). Several chats may link to one student, so a parent connects from their own phone. Each chat keeps Telegram's language (uz, ru or en; anything else is uz) and gets: a reminder about 30 minutes before each lesson with the join link (a `telegram.reminders` job the worker queues every five minutes, Tashkent time), the join link the moment the teacher starts the call, new or changed homework, an accepted or returned answer with the teacher's comment, and the monthly debtor notice alongside the auto-SMS (same switch, same month key). Delivery reuses the `telegram.send` job; a ref key per event and chat stops repeats. | A-105 | **Lesson materials and recordings (added 2026-10-06 at kai's request).** A group gets a "Materiallar" tab where whoever may mark attendance adds files (the same types and 20 MB limit as homework) and links, tied to a lesson or to the whole group, and removes them; students see everything of their group under a "Materiallar" tab on their personal link (A-101) and open files only through that link. During a video lesson the teacher can press "Record": the browser itself records (the shared screen when someone shares, else the teacher's camera, plus every microphone mixed together, 1280×720 at a modest bitrate, webm or mp4 depending on the browser) and uploads the file when recording stops or the call ends; it lands as a recording of the call's lesson, up to 400 MB, served with byte ranges so it can be scrubbed in the browser. Nothing is recorded unless the teacher presses the button, students see the red "Recording" line while it runs, and closing the tab mid-recording loses the file (the browser warns first). Students on Telegram (A-103) get one message per new material with the link to their page. | A-106 | **Online payments (added 2026-10-06 at kai's request) go through Payme and Click, each switched on under Settings → Integrations with the centre's own merchant credentials.** The student's money tab (A-101) offers "Pay online" with the debt (or one month) and the course month pre-filled; Kampus writes a pending order and sends the browser to the provider's checkout with the order id. Payme confirms through its Merchant API (JSON-RPC with `Paycom:<key>` basic auth: CheckPerform, Create, Perform, Cancel, Check, GetStatement; amounts in tiyin) and Click through SHOP API prepare and complete calls signed with md5 of the secret key; both webhooks are public endpoints protected by those credentials alone. A confirmed order becomes a regular Payment with a payment method named "Payme" or "Click" (created on first use), received by nobody, with the provider's transaction id in the comment, so reports, the student's balance, the PAYMENT_MADE auto-SMS, the staff Telegram feed and the in-app bell all behave as for a cashier's payment; the student also gets a Telegram "payment received" (A-103). A performed Payme transaction cannot be cancelled from Payme's side (refunds stay with the cashier, A-73); an unperformed one can. Uzum is not included: no verified protocol description was at hand. Nothing changes for centres that leave both providers off. | A-107 | **File retention (added 2026-10-06 at kai's request).** Lesson recordings (A-105) are deleted with their file by the nightly job once older than "Keep lesson recordings for" in Settings → Integrations → Video lessons, 90 days by default, 0 for never; each removal is audited as `material.delete` with no actor. Other uploads (homework files and answers, material files, photos) have no retention period. The nightly `backup` service mirrors the uploads volume into `./backups/uploads` (new files only, since keys are random and files never change) and keeps files deleted in Kampus for `BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS` in `./backups/uploads-deleted`; it pauses when less than 2 GB of disk would remain. The copy is on the server's own disk; off-server safety is Hetzner's server backups or a manual copy. | A-108 | **Several organisations per deployment (added 2026-10-07 at kai's request).** One Kampus server hosts several learning centres, each a separate `Organization` with its own branches, staff, students, settings catalogue, integrations and custom roles; nothing of one centre is visible to another. Every user belongs to exactly one organisation (`User.organizationId`; a phone number identifies one account, so a person working at two centres needs two numbers), and an actor's branch list is the full list of their own centre's branches when their role sees every branch, so branch checks never cross a centre. The system roles (CEO, Admin, …) are shared; custom roles belong to the centre that made them. Audit rows carry the centre; login attempts on phones no account of a centre owns are shown to nobody in that centre. Existing data was attached to the first organisation by the migration, and its first CEO became the **site owner** (`User.isSiteOwner`, a flag no role grants), the only account that may create or rename organisations, from Settings → Organisations: name, branches, and the new centre's CEO with a first password the site owner passes on in person. A new centre starts with its settings row, its branches, one cash payment method and the shared system roles; everything else its CEO adds. Integrations are per centre as well: the webhook URLs are shared, and the secret a call presents (Telegram, telephony, FaceID), the Payme key or the Click service id says which centre it is for; a student's link, the bot, the SMS gateway and the video relay settings are read through the student's branch; background jobs carry the centre in their payload or loop over every centre. | A-109 | **Opening balances and corrections (added 2026-10-09, migration kit for a centre moving to Kampus).** A `BalanceAdjustment` is a signed amount on one membership (negative = the student owes, positive = the student has money) with a kind (`OPENING` for what the student brought from the previous system, `CORRECTION` for a hand fix), a date, a comment and the cashier who entered it. The balance engine adds the membership's adjustments to its paid money before charges are subtracted, so debtor lists, the dashboard, the reminders, the reports and the portal all see it with no other change. Entering one needs `payments.create` (the student's page, "Adjust balance"), removing one needs `payments.refund`, and both are audited (`balance.adjust`, `balance.adjustRemove`) and shown in the student's history. The Students page gains "Import opening balances" (`payments.create`): one row per student and group, students matched by Kampus id, then phone, then exact name inside the chosen branch (a `branch` column may name another branch of the actor's), the group by name (optional when the student is in one group), the amount from a `balance` column in Kampus's sign or a `debt` column where positive means owes; columns are found by header in any UI language or by common aliases, else by the template's order. The first upload is a dry run that lists matched and skipped rows; a membership that already has an `OPENING` adjustment is skipped, so a file can be uploaded twice without doubling a debt. Zero rows are skipped as nothing to import. | A-110 | **Billing start separate from the join date (added 2026-10-09, migration kit).** A membership may carry a "charged from" day (`billingFrom`). When set, charging starts there instead of the activation or join date (`billingFrom ?? activatedAt ?? joinedAt`); the join date stays the real one, so lists, history and reports keep it. The field is optional in the add-member dialog, in the add-student dialog and in the group-member Excel import (a "Charged from" column appended to the template; older five-column files and files with the columns in another order still work, since member columns are now found by header like A-109), and it can be changed from the member's row menu. Changing it removes the charges of the months before the new start and of the start month itself, then re-syncs, so the start month is pro-rated again while later months keep the price and discount they were charged at. Left empty, nothing changes against A-10. Import files may also be CSV (UTF-8 or Windows-1251; comma, semicolon or tab), since other systems export CSV. | A-111 | **Catalogue imports (added 2026-10-09, migration kit).** Rooms, courses, staff, groups and parents can be imported from a spreadsheet or CSV through the same dialog as students: template download, one row per record, validation row by row, the result lists skipped rows with reasons. Columns are found by header in any UI language or by common aliases (A-109). Rooms: name, seats (10 when empty), branch. Courses: name, monthly price, months (1 when empty), description, branch. Staff (`staff.create`): name, phone, roles (by code, role name or UI label, comma-separated), branches (default: the chosen branch), gender, birth and hire dates, password; a row without a password gets a generated temporary one, returned once in the import result and never stored in clear. Groups (`groups.create`): name, course and room by name inside the branch, teacher by name or phone among teacher-role users, days as weekday words in any language or odd/even/every day, start and end time (end defaults to start + 90 minutes; a "18:00-19:30" cell works), start and end dates, status; the teacher's share follows how they are paid. Parents (`students.update`): the student by Kampus id, phone or exact name, then the parent's name and phone. Rows that already exist (same name in the branch, same phone, same parent phone on the student) are skipped, so a file can be uploaded twice. The Students page groups its three imports under one "Import" menu. | A-112 | **Debt collection (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item C1).** A `DebtCase` follows one student's debt in one branch: it opens when the student's memberships there owe money in total (archived students excluded; a debt left on a finished group still counts), carries the first unpaid month as its start, the current amount, the promise (day, amount, the debt at the time), the last staff contact and the cadence steps taken, and closes by itself when the debt is gone (Paid, Promise kept, or Left when the student was archived). Cases are reconciled whenever the list is read, inside every payment, refund and balance correction, and once a day by the worker. Staff log contacts (call, Telegram, SMS, visit, note) with an outcome; "promised to pay" pauses reminders until the promised day; the promised sum arriving reopens the ordinary cadence, the day passing marks the promise missed, counts it, tells the branch managers and flags the row for a call. The cadence is per centre (Settings → Center settings → Debt reminders, defaults 1/3/7 days, empty = off): Telegram to the student through the centre's bot, then the debtor Auto SMS (switch and text as before), then a bell task for everyone with `payments.create` in the branch when `debtTaskDays` pass without a staff contact; a contact clears the flag and restarts that count. The daily debtor SMS and monthly Telegram notice of A-88/A-103 are replaced by this cadence. The Debtors page is a main-navigation item for whoever may take payments; the dashboard debtor card and the daily debtor notice now lead there. A student who is deleted while the cases are being brought in line is skipped instead of failing the debtor list for everyone (added 2026-11-13). | A-119 | **Two-way Telegram for students and parents (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item D2).** A chat linked to a student can write to the centre's bot; the reply comes in the chat's language with a persistent three-button keyboard (Balance, Pay, Absent today) that appears when the chat links and goes when it unlinks. "Balance" (also /balance, balans, баланс) answers one line per current membership (NEW, TRIAL, ACTIVE in a group that is not archived): the balance with the next payment date, or the debt, then the coin total. "Pay" (/pay, to‘lov, оплата) creates one pending online payment per enabled provider (Payme, Click) for each membership whose suggested amount is at least 1 000 so‘m (the debt, or one month's price, for the suggested month) and answers with the checkout links, which return to the student's page; without a provider it says to pay at the centre; with nothing due it says so. "Absent today" (/absent, bugun darsga kelmaydi, сегодня не придёт; the words after the command are the reason) marks EXCUSED, with the comment "Via Telegram: <reason>" in the chat's language, every lesson of today (Tashkent) in the student's current groups that is not already PRESENT, takes back the automatic attendance coins, writes an actorless `attendance.mark` audit row and sends no auto-SMS; a PRESENT mark is reported as unchanged; with no lesson today it names the next lesson. The teacher sees the note under the name on the Today screen and as a dot with a tooltip in the attendance grid. Other text from a linked chat gets a hint with the buttons; unlinked chats are unchanged (/start and /id answer the chat id). Reports → Referral programme (permission reports.leads) counts the month's invite leads, joined friends, coins and bonuses per referrer. | A-122 | **Cashier day close (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item C3).** A `CashClose` row is one cashier's day in one branch (unique per branch, cashier and Tashkent calendar day). Closing computes, from what that cashier recorded between 00:00 and 24:00 Tashkent time by `createdAt` (not by the date typed on a payment: the money moved when the row was entered): payments received per payment method (bonuses excluded), refunds they gave, and the ledger entries they created with a method, income adding and expenses, marketing, advances and bonuses subtracting; net = payments + income − refunds − expenses. `PaymentMethod.isCash` marks the methods counted as cash (the migration marks existing methods named like naqd/cash/нал, the seed marks "Cash"); expected cash is the net of those methods, difference = counted − expected. Anyone with `payments.create` may close their own day in a branch of theirs and see and print their own closes (module Cash desk, `/cashdesk`); `finance.view` sees every close; `finance.update` accepts the hand-over (acceptedBy, acceptedAt). A day closed but not yet accepted may be closed again (the row is replaced); an accepted day may not, and a future day never. Every close is audited (`cashClose.create/update/accept`) and posted to the staff Telegram feed. Taking payments after the close is not locked. | A-123 | **Instalments and family discounts (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item C2).** A month's fee may be split into two or three `Instalment` parts, each with its own due day and amount; they must add up to the month's charge (or to the monthly price when the month is not charged yet), and the months from the first unpaid one to the next month may be split. The balance engine applies the credit to the charges in month order and, inside a split month, to its parts in due-day order; an unpaid part whose day has not come is _deferred_: it stays in the balance and the badge, but debt collection (A-112) counts only `balance + deferred`, the next payment date is the first unpaid part's day and the suggested payment is what is due now, else the next part. The parts of a month split before it is charged are listed as planned (the credit left over is applied to them) and count towards nothing until the month is charged. The daily job reminds the student once per part two days before its day, by Telegram (text `instalment`) and by the auto-SMS event INSTALMENT_DUE (off by default). Siblings are linked in a `Family` (name, percent 0–100, note; one per organisation) and students carry `familyId`. The family percent is applied as an ordinary `Discount` row per current membership (`familyId` set, 120 months, discounted price = round(base × (100 − percent) / 100)), so the fee engine, the reports and the group's Discounts tab see it, and like every discount it takes effect from the next month that is charged; the rows are replaced when the percent changes, removed when a student leaves the family (an empty family is deleted) and added when a member gets a new group (student creation, add to group, transfer, lead conversion). Fixed alongside: a current month's charge keeps the price it was created with when it is recomputed (before, a discounted current month was recomputed at the base price). | A-124 | **Staff account safety (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item F3).** A password chosen by someone else is temporary: `User.mustChangePassword` is set when an account is created or an administrator sets a new password (not when people set their own), and the migration sets it for every account that has never signed in. While it is set, the app shows only the change-password page and the API answers only the `/auth/*` endpoints; changing the password clears it, records `passwordChangedAt` and ends the person's other sessions, as does a password reset by someone else. `User.signInCode` (OFF or TELEGRAM) adds a second step to the sign-in: a six-digit code sent at once to the person's chat from Settings → Bot notifications, stored hashed in `LoginChallenge` with a five-minute life and five attempts; it can be switched on only for a person whose chat the bot knows, by the person on My account or by an administrator on the staff form, and a person whose chat is removed later signs in with the password alone. My account also lists the person's sessions by device and address with "sign out" per device and "sign out everywhere else"; administrators have "sign out of all devices" on the staff form. A sign-in from a browser and address not seen in the last 30 days is reported to the person's Telegram chat. Staff Telegram texts are Uzbek, like the staff feed (A-85). | A-125 | **Absence follow-up (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item B3).** An `AbsenceCase` follows one active student in one active group from the day they stop coming. It opens when the student's last marked lessons are `absenceStreak` absences in a row (default 2; excused lessons and lessons nobody marked are skipped), or when the group held at least two lessons in the last `absenceSilentDays` days (default 14) and the student was not marked present at one of them, whether marked absent or not marked at all; both numbers are set per centre under Centre settings and an empty field switches that rule off. Only lessons before today count, from the membership's activation (else join) date on. The case carries the rule, the lessons missed, the first day of the run (kept once set), the last present mark and the staff contacts (call, Telegram, SMS, visit or note, with the outcome no answer, will come back, ill, leaving the group or other). It closes by itself when a present mark newer than the last known one appears (RETURNED), when the membership is no longer active in an active group (LEFT) or when the rules no longer apply (CLEARED); nothing is opened or closed by hand. Cases are reconciled whenever the list is read and once a day by the worker, which tells the branch's managers (students.update) about the day's new cases in the bell; every Monday from 09:00 Tashkent the staff Telegram feed gets one Uzbek summary per branch with the week's counts and up to eight names waiting for a call, skipping branches with nothing to report. The list sits under Students in the navigation for everyone who may edit students, and Excel downloads it as shown. | A-126 | **Lead follow-up (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item B5).** A lead may carry an owner (`Lead.ownerId`, a staff member who holds `leads.update` in the branch) and a next-contact date. Each day from 09:00 Tashkent the `leads.followUp` job writes one bell notice per owner with due leads and, when the owner's chat is listed under Bot notifications, one Telegram message naming up to eight of them; leads without an owner are announced to the branch's `leads.update` holders. Dates are compared with the Tashkent calendar day. | A-134 | **Monitoring and alerts (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item F5).** The server keeps a few facts about itself in `SystemState` (one row per key: the worker's last tick, written every tick; the backup's last run, written by `docker/backup.sh` through `psql` after each dump, with file, size and the backup disk's free space, or a `backup.error` row when `pg_dump` fails; the alert recipient; one row per open alert) and `SystemEvent` (HTTP 500s recorded by the route wrapper, at most one per second per process; alerts sent; pruned after 7 days). The site owner (A-108) sees a **Server status** card above Settings → Organisations: application uptime, database latency, worker (red after 3 minutes of silence), job queue (waiting, overdue, failed in 24 h with the last error), backup (attention after 26 hours or a failed attempt; "no data" until the backup container's first run on this version), the disk of `UPLOAD_DIR` via `statfs` (attention under 2 GB, red under 512 MB) and server errors of the last 24 hours (attention at 5 in 15 minutes); `GET /api/v1/system/status`, `POST /api/v1/system/check`. Alerts go to one Telegram chat ID (`PUT /api/v1/system/alerts`, `POST /api/v1/system/alerts/test`), sent by the site owner's own organisation bot, in English with a "Kampus server" prefix: the pass runs at most every 5 minutes per app process, clocked by Docker's 30-second poll of `/api/v1/health`, so the app watches the worker rather than the worker itself; a new alert is sent at once, an open one repeated every 6 hours, and a "resolved" message follows when the rule stops firing. No external uptime service is involved; `/api/v1/health` stays the endpoint one would point such a service at. Open: whether alerts should also go to the CEO of every hosted centre (currently site owner only). | A-135 | **Shared Telegram bot (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item F6).** The site owner's Telegram card has a switch **Shared with every centre on this server** (`sharedWithAllCentres`, dropped from anyone else's save). `telegramConfigFor(db, organizationId)` is the one accessor: a centre's own enabled bot (token, username or webhook secret set) wins; otherwise the shared bot of the flagged, enabled configuration, with the centre's own weekly-report preference when it has a Telegram row. Notifier, portal connect link, weekly report and the setup checklist use it, so a new centre gets Telegram on day one without BotFather. The webhook still finds the bot by its secret (A-108); when that bot is shared, the update is routed by the chat instead of the bot: `/start <code>` links a student of any centre, `/stop` unlinks any chat, and balance, pay and absence replies are about the linked student's own centre. Decided by kai on 2026-11-10 ("all branches should use the same bot"): the switch is on on the live server, so every centre without a bot of its own uses the site owner's bot, Telegram login included (A-179).
