| A-137 | **Course syllabus and lesson topics (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item B9).** A course can carry a syllabus: an ordered list of topics (`CourseTopic`, title and optional note), edited from **Syllabus** in the course's row menu as one title per line (`settings.catalog`); a title that stays keeps its row, so lessons already linked to it stay linked. A lesson may point at one topic (`Lesson.courseTopicId`) besides its free-text topic; the free text wins when both are set. When attendance is first marked on a lesson that has neither, the lesson takes the group's next uncovered topic (the first topic no lesson of the group points at), so the syllabus advances by itself; Today shows that next topic on a topic-less lesson with a **Use it** button, the lesson topic dialog offers the topics in a list, and the group has a **Syllabus** tab (`groups.view`) with covered / next / planned per topic and the covering lesson's date. The student page shows the syllabus title where there is no free text and the next topic before the next lesson. Topics are per course, not per group: a group that skips a topic can set it by hand later or leave it. Supersedes the "left out" part of A-18 for topics only. | A-138 | **Waiting list (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item B6).** `WaitlistEntry` holds a person (name, phone, optional link to a lead or a student) waiting for a course in a branch, with preferred days and time, a note and a status (waiting, offered, enrolled, declined, removed); entries queue per branch and course in the order they were added, and the list page under Leads shows each person's place. Entries come from a lead card ("Add to waiting list", prefilled) or the list page; the same phone cannot wait twice for one course. **Offer seats to the waiting list** on a group (`leads.update`) takes the group's free seats (the smallest room capacity on its schedule minus NEW/TRIAL/ACTIVE members; unlimited when no slot has a room) and offers them to the first waiting entries of the group's course and branch: each gets the auto-SMS `WAITLIST_OFFER` (a new switch under Auto SMS, off by default like the others, with the new `{days}` variable) when that switch is on, a Telegram message when the entry is a linked student, and becomes OFFERED with the group recorded; the dialog says beforehand whether the SMS is on. **Enrol** adds the person to a group of the entry's course through the existing paths (a lead via leads-to-group, which converts it; a student as a member; anyone else as a new student) and closes the entry; declined and removed entries stay in the history and can be put back to waiting. Offers are a manager's action, not automatic: a group opening does not text anyone by itself. | A-139 | **Attendance by QR (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item B8).** The badges' QR codes (`kampus:student:<id>`, A-65) are now read: `/today/scan` opens the camera (the browser's BarcodeDetector where it exists, jsQR as the fallback) and a text field for a hand scanner, which types the code and Enter on its own. `POST /attendance/scan` (`groups.attendance.mark`) looks the student up in the user's branches and marks them present through the normal attendance path (so coins, auto-SMS and the percentage follow): on the lesson the page was opened for from a Today card, else on the student's lesson of the day in a group the user may mark, the one under way (30 minutes of slack either side), else the next one today, else the last one. | A-140 | **Certificates of graduation (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item G2).** A graduated membership can carry one `Certificate`: a number sequential per organisation and year (`2026-0001`), a title (the course name by default), a level (the CEFR level of the graduate record by default), the issue date, who issued it and a public code. Staff with the students permission issue it from the graduates report (**Issue certificate**) and open `/certificates/<id>`, a signed-in landscape A4 sheet with the centre's logo and name, the branch, the student's name, the title and level, the course dates and group, the teacher and director signature lines, the number and a QR code; the browser's print dialog makes the PDF, as for receipts and badges. The QR code and the link point at `/cert/<code>`, public and not indexed, which shows the organisation, the student's name, the title, level, date and number and whether the certificate is valid, revoked or unknown; nothing more. **Revoke** keeps the row and the paper but makes the public page say "revoked"; a revoked certificate can be issued again under the same number with a new code. The student is told on Telegram with the link when one is issued, and their personal page lists their valid certificates under Results. No file is stored: the sheet is rendered from the row each time. | A-142 | **Archived students and payment history import (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item A5).** The optional second pass of a migration. **Import archived students** (Students → Import; `students.create`) takes one row per student who had already left: name, phone, group, join and leave dates, reason, note. Each becomes a `Student` with `isArchived` and, when a group of the branch is named, a `GroupMembership` with status `ARCHIVED`, `joinedAt`, `leftAt` and the free-text `leaveReason`, so the churn report (A-56) counts them. Rows whose phone (or, without a phone, whose exact name) already belongs to a student of the branch are skipped, so a file can be uploaded twice. **Import payment history** (`payments.create`) takes one row per payment of the previous system: student (Kampus ID, phone or exact name, archived students included), group name, amount, date, method, comment. Each becomes a `LegacyPayment`, a plain record that no balance, debtor list, cash report or receipt reads; the student's page lists them under the payment history as **Payments in the previous system**, and the refund permission can remove a row. A row with the same student, date, amount and group is skipped. Both importers preview first (`dryRun`) like the opening-balance import (A-109). | A-143 | **SOFF CRM importer (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item A4).** Settings → **Import from SOFF CRM** (`students.create` to open; each file needs the permission of the Kampus importer it feeds) takes the vendor's own Excel exports one at a time. `detectSoffFile` recognises the list by its header row (Uzbek labels as the vendor's screens show them, plus English and Russian variants): staff (Ism familiya, Telefon raqam, Kasbi, Ishga olingan sana…), groups (Guruh nomi, Kurs, O'qituvchi, Dars kunlari, Dars vaqti, Ochilgan, Yakunlanadi, Status), students (Ism familiya, Telefon, Guruhlar, Balans…) and student payments (Sana, Summa, Qaytarilgan summa, Guruh, To'lov turi, Qaysi oy uchun…). | A-147 | **Online fiscal receipts (added 2026-10-09, round 2 item C6).** Uzbekistan's online cash registers are reached through an OFD provider whose API differs per provider and is chosen by the centre's accountant, so Kampus talks to one small contract (`FiscalProvider.issue`: kind, reference, amount, payment type cash/card, INN, cash register id, VAT, MXIK code, items) with two adapters: `HttpFiscalProvider` (`POST {apiUrl}/receipts` with a bearer key, answer `{id, fiscalSign, url?, qrUrl?}`) when Settings → Integrations → Fiscal receipts has an address and key, else `FakeFiscalProvider` (in-memory, deterministic sign) so the flow can be tried before a contract exists. With the integration on and **auto-issue** on, `createPayment` and `refundPayment` file a `FiscalReceipt` row (SALE or REFUND, PENDING) inside their transaction and queue a `fiscal.issue` job (unique per receipt, retried with the queue's backoff); the job stores ISSUED with the provider's number, sign and receipt URL or FAILED with the error. The printed receipt shows the fiscal number, sign and a QR of the provider's receipt page; payment tables show a **Fiscal receipt** column (Pending / Issued / Failed, with a retry that also files a receipt for a payment made while auto-issue was off, `POST /api/v1/payments/<id>/fiscal`, permission `payments.create`), shown only when at least one listed payment has a receipt. Online payments (A-106) are not fiscalised by Kampus because Payme and Click issue the fiscal receipt themselves. Open: the real provider's API shape and credentials (Hakimbek's accountant); the item name sent is "course · group", one line at the full amount, VAT from the setting. | A-150 | **Students and parents sign in with Telegram (added 2026-11-05, online-lessons plan items A1-A4 and B9).** Students and parents get their own sign-in at `/student` without a password and without self-registration. **Log in with Telegram** runs Telegram's OpenID Connect flow (authorization code with PKCE S256 at `oauth.telegram.org`, scopes `openid profile phone`, client secret sent as HTTP Basic); the ID token is verified against Telegram's JWKS (RS256 or ES256, issuer `https://oauth.telegram.org`, audience the Client ID, not expired, issued at most 10 minutes ago, nonce checked when present) and only a phone with `phone_number_verified` other than false is used. The Client ID and Client Secret come from BotFather → the bot → Login Widget after the bot is switched to OpenID Connect login (the exact steps are in A-179) and are entered in Settings → Integrations → Telegram (`loginClientId`, `loginClientSecret`, the secret masked). **Matching:** a `StudentAccount` (one per Telegram user id) is created or updated only when the Telegram-verified phone, normalised to `+998…`, equals the phone of a non-archived, non-blacklisted student or of a parent of a non-archived student, or when the account already holds a link; otherwise the sign-in is refused with nothing written. Each match becomes a `StudentAccountLink` (one per student record and one per parent record, so a record already held by another Telegram account is skipped and reported as "linked elsewhere"; staff remove the old link first). Opening the student's own connect link in the bot (`/start <code>`, A-103) also links that Telegram account to the student (`via CODE`), which covers a student whose Telegram phone differs from the phone on file. **Which bot:** on a centre's own domain (A-114) the centre's effective bot (its own or the shared one, A-135) and only that centre's people; on the server's own address the site owner's shared bot when it has login credentials, matching across every centre, else the only centre with login credentials; nothing otherwise. **From the bot:** `/start login` or `/login` shows a one-time keyboard with a contact button; a contact whose `user_id` equals the sender is the sender's Telegram-verified phone and is matched the same way; a match gets a single-use sign-in link valid 10 minutes (`StudentLoginTicket`, `/api/v1/student-auth/enter/<ticket>`), and the chat is linked for notices (A-103) when it was not linked yet. **Sessions:** cookie `kampus_student` (httpOnly, SameSite Lax), separate from the staff session, 30 days sliding; a session stops working when its links lead only to archived or blacklisted students or suspended centres (A-144). The student home `/student` lists every linked student (their own record first, then children) with current groups, next lesson, a Join button while the group's video lesson is live, balance, unread news and homework of the last 21 days not yet answered or returned; each group opens the existing personal page `/class/<token>`, whose token stays the credential for the page's own actions, so personal links keep working unchanged. Sign out and sign out on all devices are plain form posts with a same-origin check. **Staff:** the student's page shows **Kampus app sign-in**: the accounts linked to the student and to their parents, with how and when, last visit and device count; `students.update` may sign an account out everywhere or remove its access (audited as `student.account.*`). Removing access does not stop the same phone from matching again at the next sign-in, so a wrong phone is corrected on the card first. Tests use a fake provider that is switched on only by `TELEGRAM_LOGIN_FAKE=1` (CI), never on the server. | A-151 | **Attendance from a video call (added 2026-11-05, online-lessons item B1).** A call that belongs to a lesson proposes that lesson's attendance from who was in the call: minutes online are summed over a student's reconnects (a still-live call counts up to now, an ended one up to each participant's last sign of life); a member with at least `attendanceMinutes` (Settings → Integrations → Video lessons, 1-120, default 10) is proposed present, everyone else absent. Lateness is measured from the lesson's start time in Tashkent time (UTC+5); a present mark for someone who joined later than the threshold carries the note `+N min`. Nothing is written by itself: the teacher opens **Attendance from the call** on the group's video card (during the call or from the last call), changes what is wrong and applies; marks already set by hand are shown and kept unless the teacher picks them again. Applying goes through the normal attendance path (permission `groups.attendance.mark`, the lesson-day rule, coins, absence SMS, audit). A call without a lesson (started on a day without one) has no attendance to apply. | A-152 | **Hand queue, spotlight, focus mode and reactions in video lessons (added 2026-11-05, online-lessons items B5 and B6).** **Hand queue:** the server stores when each raised hand went up (`VideoParticipant.handRaisedAt`, kept while the hand stays up, cleared when it goes down), so everyone sees the same order: a number on the hand mark and a Raised hands list at the top of People. The teacher (HOST) can lower one person's hand (`lower` signal); the student sees who lowered it. **Spotlight:** the teacher picks one person (themselves included) whom every screen shows large; it is stored on the room (`VideoRoom.spotlightId`) so late joiners get it, and falls away when that person leaves. A person's own pin still wins on their own screen. **Focus mode:** stored on the room (`VideoRoom.focusMode`); students then see only the teacher, the spotlight, a shared screen and themselves; other students stay audible. Staff see everyone. Only the HOST's browser may change the stage (the sync request's `room` field is ignored from anyone else) and only the HOST may send `mute` and `lower`. **Reactions:** thumbs up, clap, heart, laugh and wow float on the sender's picture for 4 seconds on every screen; a student's "slower" and "faster" go only to the teacher and staff, who see a tally of each student's latest vote in the last minute. Reactions are not stored. | A-153 | **Polls in video lessons (added 2026-11-05, online-lessons item B2).** The teacher (HOST) opens a question with 2-6 answers from the Poll panel; one poll is open per call and opening another closes the previous. Only students answer, one answer each (keyed by student, so a rejoin keeps it), changeable while the poll is open; a guest's or staff's answer is ignored. While open, the counts and who answered what are shown to the teacher and staff only; students see their own answer. Closing shows the counts to everyone (names stay with staff). Poll actions travel in the browsers' regular sync, so a student needs nothing beyond the call; a student's open/close request is ignored by the server. | A-162 | **Gradebook with weighted categories (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item C8).** Each course carries `gradeWeights` JSON `{lessons, homework, exercises, tests, exams}` (integers summing to 100; null = defaults 30/30/0/20/20). | A-165 | **Vocabulary trainer (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item C5).** `VocabWord` rows hang off a `CourseTopic` (term, translation, optional example, at most 200 per topic), edited by whoever may edit the topic's content (A-157) as "term — translation — example" lines; an edit keeps the row (and the students' progress) when the term stays. Students see the words of their open topics (same rule as content and exercises) as flashcards: `VocabCard` per membership and word with a Leitner box 0-5; a known word moves up one box and is due again after 0, 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, a missed word drops to box 0 and is due in 10 minutes; box 4 and above counts as learned. A session serves up to 20 cards, due reviews first then new words in syllabus order. `VocabDay` counts the student's reviews per Tashkent calendar day; a streak is consecutive days ending today or yesterday. Every 7th day of a streak awards the `VOCAB_STREAK` coin event (new, default 15 coins, follows the auto-coins switch and rules in Settings → Coins) once per day via refKey `vocab:<membershipId>:<day>`. Badges `words50` (50 learned words) and `vocabStreak7` (a 7-day streak) join A-163. | A-166 | **Students move or cancel their own 1:1 lessons (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item D2).** Off by default; Settings → General has the switch **Students may move or cancel their own 1:1 lessons** and the notice in hours (`OrgSettings.studentReschedule`, `studentRescheduleHours`, 1–168, default 12). It applies only to a group with exactly one current member (NEW, TRIAL or ACTIVE). The student's Schedule tab lists the next ten lessons; inside the window (lesson start minus the notice, Tashkent time) and while the lesson has neither attendance nor grades, the student may **move** it to a new date and time or **cancel** it (`POST /api/v1/public/class/:token/schedule/:lessonId/move                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | cancel`, the link is the credential). A new time must be ahead, inside the centre's working hours and must not overlap another lesson of the group or of its teachers (`validation.outsideWorkHours`, `validation.teacherBusy`). A move reuses the day-off model of A-117: a `GroupDayOff`with reason`@student.moved`and`movedToLessonId`pointing at the extra lesson, so the staff list shows **Moved by the student** and the teacher's undo still works; moving an already moved lesson updates it in place. A cancellation deletes the lesson and leaves a day off with reason`@student.cancelled`. A day off without a new time (the teacher's or the student's own) is listed on the student's page under **Lessons waiting for a new time** and can be **rebooked** at any time (`POST .../schedule/rebook/:dayOffId`), which sets `movedToLessonId`. Students and parents are told through `notifyLessonChange`(Telegram, auto-SMS) and the branch's staff recipients get a bot line; everything is audited with no actor as`lesson.studentMove`, `lesson.studentCancel`, `lesson.studentRebook`. Later than the window the lesson stays and counts as held; the office changes it as before. |
| A-167 | **No-show in a 1:1 call (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item D3).** Settings → Integrations → Video lessons gets **Minutes alone before a 1:1 no-show is recorded** (`noShowMinutes`, 0–60, default 15; 0 off). While the teacher's browser syncs a LIVE room that belongs to a lesson of a group with exactly one current, non-archived member, and no student browser has ever joined, once the teacher has waited that long since the later of the call's start and the lesson's start (Tashkent time) `checkNoShow` records `VideoRoom.noShowAt` (an atomic claim, once per room), marks the student ABSENT through `markAttendance` as the teacher who opened the room (so coins, auto-SMS to parents and the audit log behave like a hand mark; an existing mark is left alone), sends the student's Telegram chats `telegramBot.noShow`, posts a line to the branch's staff bot recipients and returns the time in the sync, which the teacher sees as a banner (`video.room.noShow`). A student who joins afterwards is handled by attendance from the call (A-151), which may change the mark. Group lessons are untouched. | A-168 | **Post-lesson rating and the teacher's note (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item D6).** A lesson carries an optional `studentNote` (≤ 1000 characters) set through the lesson update (`PATCH /api/v1/lessons/:id`, attendance right) from the topic dialog of the attendance grid or the Lesson panel of a call; it is shown on the students' pages under the lesson and a new or changed note is sent to the group's current students on Telegram (`telegramBot.lessonNote`, text cut at 500). Students rate a lesson from their page (`LessonRating`, one per lesson and membership, 1–5 and an optional line ≤ 500; `POST /api/v1/public/class/:token/lessons/:lessonId/rating`, upsert, audited with no actor as `lesson.rate`) once its end time has passed in Tashkent time and the student is not marked ABSENT (`errors.lessonNotOver`, `errors.ratingAbsent`); a rating can be changed later. Staff who see the group get the average and count per lesson in the month grid (`LessonDto.rating`) and the names, stars and lines in the lesson dialog (`GET /api/v1/lessons/:id/ratings`). Ratings are not anonymous: in a 1:1 group they could not be, and the teacher is meant to answer them. | A-169 | **Teacher booking hours and self-booking (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item D1).** A teacher keeps weekly windows (`TeacherAvailability`, up to 21, no overlap within a day) in which their 1:1 students may book or move lessons: edited by the teacher on My account and by anyone with `teachers.update` on the teacher's page (`GET/PUT /api/v1/teachers/:id/availability`, audited as `staff.availability`). For a group under the A-166 rules the student's schedule carries `hasAvailability` and the **free slots** of the next 14 days: the group's main teachers' windows cut into the centre's schedule step (`scheduleStepMinutes`) as slots of the group's usual lesson length, minus every lesson of the group or of those teachers (main or support), the group's days off without a new time and the branch's days off, future only, at most 60. **Book** (`POST /api/v1/public/class/:token/schedule/book`) creates an extra lesson (`isExtra`, no `movedFrom`) after the A-166 checks; when the teachers keep windows, any new time (book, move, rebook) must lie inside one (`validation.outsideAvailability`); without windows the student types any free time inside the centre's hours. At most two extra lessons without `movedFrom` may wait ahead per group (`errors.bookingLimit`), which also counts the office's own extra lessons. The student and parents get `telegramBot.lessonBooked`, the branch's staff recipients a bot line; audited with no actor as `lesson.studentBook`. | A-170 | **Group chat with a Telegram mirror (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item E1).** Each group has one chat (`GroupChatMessage`: `userId` for staff, `membershipId` for a student, `source` WEB or TELEGRAM). Staff with `groups.view` on the group read and write it from the **Chat** tab (`GET`/`POST /api/v1/groups/:id/chat`, `POST …/chat/read`); students from the **Chat** tab of their link (`/api/v1/public/class/:token/chat`). Unread = messages by others since `GroupChatRead.readAt` (staff) or `GroupMembership.chatReadAt` (student). A staff message is mirrored to every linked Telegram chat of the group's current members (`telegramBot.chatMessage`) and sets `StudentTelegramChat.chatGroupId` to that group; a plain message a linked chat sends to the bot (anything `parseBotCommand` does not recognise) is posted into the chat of `chatGroupId`, or of the student's only group, and when the student is in several groups and none has spoken the bot offers them as `💬 <name>` buttons and remembers the pick. Students' messages (web or Telegram) are copied in Uzbek to the group's teachers who are bot recipients (`telegramBot.chatFromStudent`). Archived groups are read-only and never a Telegram target. The call room's own live chat is separate and not stored. | A-171 | **Lesson summary to parents after each online lesson (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item E2).** When a video room closes (the host ends it, it runs out of time or sits empty), `closeRoom` queues a `lesson.summary` job for 30 minutes later (`SUMMARY_DELAY_MS`, unique per room), time for the teacher to mark attendance and set homework. The job sends every current member of the group one `telegramBot.lessonSummary` message to each of their linked chats, in the chat's language: group, date and time, the lesson's topic (`Lesson.topic`, else the syllabus topic's title, else "not written down"), the student's attendance (present / absent / excused / not marked yet) and the homework (title and the first 120 characters of the text, with the due date), or "none". Rooms without a lesson and archived groups send nothing; the Telegram card's **Summary to parents after each online lesson** switch (`lessonSummary`, default on; a centre on the shared bot keeps its own value) turns it off per centre. Idempotent per room and student, so a retried job sends nothing twice. | A-172 | **Trial visitor's own link into the online lesson (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item D5).** Every trial booking (A-131) gets a `videoToken`; the lead card's **Copy the visitor's lesson link** copies `/class/trial/<token>`, and a lead with a Telegram inbox chat (A-146) receives the link there when the trial is booked (`telegramBot.trialLink`, with an OUT copy in the inbox). | A-175 | **Streaming copies of recordings and the video player (added 2026-11-06, online-lessons item F3).** A recording is one WebM/MP4 file as the teacher's browser made it; iPhones cannot play WebM and weak connections stall on it. When Settings → Integrations → Video lessons → "Make streaming copies of recordings" is on (`hlsRecordings`, default off because it costs CPU), `saveRecording` enqueues `recording.hls` and the worker (`hls.service.ts`, ffmpeg in the worker image, `FFMPEG_PATH`/`FFPROBE_PATH` overrides) writes HLS: H.264/AAC renditions 360p and 720p (never taller than the source), each one fMP4 media file whose init section and segments are byte ranges, plus a playlist, and a master playlist, all under `hls/` keys in the same storage (A-48/A-174); `LessonMaterial.hlsKey` points at the master, `hlsKeys` lists every file for deletion. Heavy jobs run in a lane of their own in the worker (one at a time, low OS priority, claim renewed every 4 minutes) so reminders are never held up; `POST /api/v1/jobs/run` skips them. Files are served like uploads through `/api/v1/files` and the student link only. The shared `VideoPlayer` plays HLS natively on Safari and through hls.js elsewhere, falls back to the file, remembers the speed (0.75–2×) in the browser and continues where the viewer stopped: students' positions are stored per membership in `MaterialView` (`POST /api/v1/public/class/:token/materials/:id/progress`, every 10 s, on pause and end; 90 % counts as watched) so another device continues too, and staff see "N opened, M watched to the end" under each recording. Staff previews and self-study videos remember the position in the browser only. | A-178 | **Lesson packages (added 2026-11-09, online-lessons item D4).** A group has a `billingMode`: `MONTHLY` (the course price per month, as before) or `PACKAGES`. A package group sells `LessonPackage`s (name, lessons, price; deactivated when sold at least once instead of deleted) from a Packages tab; no monthly charges are written for it. Selling a package (`POST /api/v1/groups/:id/packages/sell`, permission `payments.create`) writes one ordinary Payment of the package price (receipt, SMS, feed, fiscal receipt as for any payment) and a `PackagePurchase` copying the name, lessons and price, in one transaction. Every PRESENT mark in a package group writes a `PackageUse` on the member's oldest purchase with credits left; with none left the use has no purchase (the lesson is owed) and the next purchase takes over the owed uses, oldest first. Changing the mark away from PRESENT removes the use. Credits = lessons bought − uses (negative = owed); shown as "N lessons left" on the member list, the student's group card and the student's own page, which also lists the packages on offer. The balance of a package member is payments − purchases (plus any months charged before a switch to packages); `nextPaymentDate` is null unless a debt exists, and the pay dialog suggests the cheapest package. The student gets one Telegram line (`packageLow`) when a mark leaves them one or zero lessons. Open: online purchase of a package from the student page, refunds of unused credits, and packages shared across groups. | A-179 | **Setting up Telegram login in BotFather (added 2026-11-10, after the first live setup).** What A-150 needs from Telegram, as BotFather offers it today: in @BotFather's app choose the bot → **Login Widget** and switch the bot to **OpenID Connect** login. Staff do not sign in with Telegram: they keep phone and password, with the optional Telegram code at sign-in. The in-app help (Integrations → Students sign in with Telegram) carries the same steps in uz, ru and en. The labels of the **Make streaming copies of recordings** switch and its note (A-175) were missing from the message files and were added on the same day. | A-180 | **Staff sign in with Telegram, and a centre can refuse passwords (added 2026-11-10 at kai's request: "login should happen only with telegram").** The staff sign-in page shows **Log in with Telegram** whenever the address has a Telegram login (A-150, `resolveLoginSetup`). `GET /api/v1/auth/telegram/start` sends the browser to Telegram with a state cookie marked `kind: "staff"`; Telegram returns to the callback BotFather already knows (`/api/v1/student-auth/telegram/callback`), which tells staff and student logins apart by that state, so nothing is added in BotFather and a code asked for on one page never opens the other kind of session. **Matching:** the Telegram-verified phone, normalised to `+998…`, must equal `User.phone` (unique on the server) of a non-archived staff member; on a centre's own address only that centre's staff; a suspended centre keeps everyone but the site owner out. Nobody is created or linked. A miss is logged in the login log and answers "no staff member has this number". The Telegram code of A-124 is not asked for after a Telegram sign-in, since Telegram is the proof. `Session.signedInWith` and `LoginLog.method` (`PASSWORD` or `TELEGRAM`) record how the person came in; a Telegram session is never sent to the change-password page. **Telegram only:** `OrgSettings.staffTelegramOnly` (Settings → General → Staff sign-in, off by default). With it on, `login()` refuses a correct password with "your centre signs in with Telegram only" (a wrong password still reads as wrong, so the answer gives nothing away), new staff may be created without a password (the account gets a random one nobody knows), and the sign-in page drops the password form once every centre the address serves has switched. **Against lock-out:** the switch can be turned on only from a session opened with Telegram and only when the centre's bot, own or shared, has login keys; turning it off is always allowed; a save that leaves the field out keeps it. Passwords are accepted again by themselves when the bot has no login keys, and always when the server runs with `STAFF_PASSWORD_LOGIN=on` (DEPLOY.md, Troubleshooting). Passwords are not deleted, so switching back restores the old sign-in. Open: sign-in from inside the bot for staff (students have it), and showing the method in the login log page. | A-181 | **Telegram only for every centre at once (added 2026-11-12 at kai's request: "everybody should login with telegram only").** A-180's switch is per centre, so on the server's own address the password form stayed until every centre had switched, each from its own CEO's Telegram session. The site owner now has a second switch in Settings → General → Staff sign-in, **Every centre on this server signs in with Telegram only** (`OrgSettings.staffTelegramOnlyAll`, kept only when the site owner saves it, like the shared bot flag of A-135). Other centres see their own switch on and locked with a line saying the site owner set it. **Assumed:** the rule is one for the whole server, with no per-centre exception; staff whose Telegram number differs from the phone on their staff card are refused until the phone is corrected in Settings → Staff (the hint under the switch says so). | A-182 | **Video lessons on tablets, and screen sharing where the browser has none (added 2026-11-12 after kai's iPad screenshot: "platform should be tablet friendly … no screenshare option").** The room showed **Share screen** only where `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia` exists; Safari on iPad and iPhone (and every other iPad browser, which all run Safari's engine) lacks it up to iPadOS 26, and Apple added it in iPadOS 27 (September 2026), so an updated iPad shows the normal button and nothing else changes there. Where the API is missing, the button stays in the bar (`share-unavailable-button`) and opens a notice (`video.room.shareUnavailable`) with what works instead: **Open the whiteboard** (host only, A-155), **Show the lesson's materials** (the Lesson panel, A-154) and **Switch camera**. `CallEngine.switchCamera()` lists the browser's video inputs once (`enumerateDevices`), and when there is more than one and no screen is being shared, a **Switch camera** button sits in the bar for everyone: it stops the current camera first (phones allow one open camera at a time), opens the next one by `deviceId` with the role's picture size (`cameraConstraints`, the same as the lobby), falls back to the camera it had, and swaps the track on every peer connection the way screen sharing does, keeping the camera-off state. The camera is not remembered between calls. Touch sizes: header buttons, the whiteboard tools and the picture's pin button grow or show on coarse pointers (`pointer-coarse:`), so a finger reaches them; the share button is no longer hidden on narrow screens. The rest of the app needed no change at iPad sizes (checked at 820×1180 and 1180×820 with touch: drawer menu below 1024 px, sidebar above, side-sheet dialogs, tables scroll sideways). camera). | A-183 | **Show a material to everyone in a video lesson (added 2026-11-12 on kai's word: "let's add show this material to everyone and anything else needed for screensharing. it should be compatiable and confortable to be used by all devices and any missing features you should add").** Screen sharing needs `getDisplayMedia`, which phones and older iPads lack (A-182), so this puts content on every screen without it. The teacher (HOST) presses **Show a file to everyone** in the bar (`toggle-present`, opens the Lesson panel) and picks a file from the device (PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP, audio or video up to 20 MB, uploaded through `/uploads/documents` and saved as a `LessonMaterial` of the call's lesson, or of the group when the call has none; title = file name without extension) or presses the show button next to a listed material. `VideoRoom.shownMaterial` (JSON `{ id, page, playing, position, at }`, additive migration `20261112160000_video_shown_material`) is set only by the host through the stage part of the sync call (`room.material`: an object shows or updates, `null` stops, left out keeps); another group's material is ignored, a deleted one leaves the stage. Each sync answer carries `stage.material` with the URL as that participant may open it (students get the copy behind their personal link) and `now`, the server clock. Display by kind and file extension (`materialView`, `src/lib/video-material.ts`): a **PDF** is drawn page by page with pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist` 6.5.438 legacy build, loaded only when needed; worker in `public/pdfjs/`, copied by `scripts/copy-pdf-worker.mjs`, a unit test fails on a stale copy) because iPhones and iPads show only page one of an embedded PDF; the teacher turns pages (buttons or arrow keys) and everyone follows. A **picture** is shown whole. A **video or audio file** (or a recording) plays in step: the teacher's player has the controls, each play, pause and jump is stored, followers work out the position from the server clock and seek only when more than 1.5 s off, checking every 4 s; a browser that refuses to start sound shows one **Tap to play** button. A **YouTube link** is embedded and each person starts it (not kept in step). **Other links and Word, PowerPoint, Excel or zip files** are a card with an **Open** button, so slides are best saved as PDF. **Pen over a page:** with a PDF or picture shown the pen draws over it; strokes carry a `layer` (empty = whiteboard, `m:<materialId>:<page>` = one page) in 0-1 coordinates of a box that keeps the page's shape, so marks land on the same spot on every screen; each page keeps its marks, undo and clear work per layer, **Let students draw** applies as in A-155. A recording made meanwhile draws the shown page, picture or video in place of the stage. Not built: play-in-step for YouTube; Word or PowerPoint as pages (needs a server converter); a laser pointer; the sound of a played audio or video file in the recording (its picture is recorded). Tests: `tests/unit/video-material.test.ts`, the shown-material case in `video.services.test.ts`, and "a teacher shows a file to everyone" in `tests/e2e/video.spec.ts` (teacher on a tablet without screen capture, student on a phone). | A-189 | **A whole centre is copied from SOFF CRM in one run (added 2026-11-13 on kai's words: "copy all the data from https://kingston.soffcrm.uz/ to kingston").** The first migration of that centre (9 October) brought courses, rooms, staff, groups and active students through the Excel imports (A-109 to A-111, A-143). It left out the archived students, attendance, leads, finance, exams, comments and the balances, and the centre kept working in the old system for another month, whose licence ends on 20 November. **What is copied:** staff (active and archived), courses, rooms, groups with schedule and teacher, students with parents and comments, every membership with its real join and leave dates, status (active, new, frozen, archived, graduated), personal price and leave reason, the balance per membership, the payment history (A-142 history rows; a refund is a negative row), attendance (present, absent, late as a comment), leads on boards with the old columns, expenses and income by category, advances, bonuses, fines and marketing spend, and group exams. **How:** `soff-export-normalize.ts` is pure and turns the raw export files (one per branch, the old API's read-only answers) into one snapshot; `soff-export-apply.ts` writes the snapshot into one organisation; `scripts/import-soff-export.ts` runs both on the server (`docs/DEPLOY.md` section 11). **Decisions:** (1) One transaction; a dry run is the same run rolled back, so its report is exact. (2) Writes go straight to the database, so nothing sends an SMS or Telegram message, gives coins or notifies anyone. (3) Idempotent: every copied record is remembered in the new `ImportRef` table, existing records are matched first (`soff-export-match.ts`, pure: staff by phone; courses and rooms by name; students by phone and name, then by a phone or a name that one student has on each side; groups by the students they share, because the centre renamed its groups and one group's old name was another's new one, and only then by name or an earlier name from the old system's history; a person the old system holds twice under one phone and name is told apart by the groups). A rehearsal against the list of what the October migration wrote paired all 38 groups and all 390 students with the right record, and a second run adds, updates and, for payments and finance rows, removes what is gone in the old system. (4) The old system is the truth for what it holds: a matched student, group or membership is brought in line with it. Kampus records it does not know are left alone and counted in the report. (5) A student may sit in the same group several times in the old system; Kampus allows one membership per group and student, so the stays are folded into one (the current stay wins, earlier ones go into the note, balances are added up). (6) **Balances:** the old balance of each membership becomes one OPENING adjustment (A-109), `billingFrom` (A-110) is the old system's next payment day, and Kampus charges for months before it are deleted; a member who left is charged nothing; a frozen member is frozen from the day of the copy. The report shows owed and credit totals per branch as the old system has them beside what Kampus's own balance engine computes after the copy; they must be equal. (7) A student of two branches becomes one record in each branch. (8) Expense rows carry no branch in the old system, but their category belongs to one branch's budget, so each row goes to that branch; marketing rows carry their own branch. (9) New staff accounts get their old role except CEO, a random password nobody knows and the must-change flag; archived staff are created archived; a phone that already signs in to another centre is skipped and reported. (10) Not copied: photos and grades (the old system has none), coins (all zero), passwords, the amoCRM connection, SMS templates and history, the action log and salary sheets. Exam scores per student are not in the export yet. **Tests:** `tests/unit/soff-export.test.ts` (18) with a made-up export: folding of stays, groups that swapped names, a person held twice, branch of an expense, dry run writes nothing, the real run equals the dry run, balances equal the old system's by Kampus's engine, a second run changes nothing, a later copy updates a balance and removes a payment. One additive migration (`ImportRef`). | A-190 | **A daily summary for the person who opens Kampus (added 2026-11-13 on kai's words: "you see how ai summary is provided in soffcrm when ceo opens a page, i would like smth like that in the ui for ceo, branch manager and teachers as well, based on who opens, info related to them").** The old CRM greets its director with "yesterday's report": figures of the day and a short AI conclusion. Kampus now has its own for every staff member who has the Home page or the Today page. **Who sees what:** two views. _Centre_ (permission `dashboard.view`): the whole centre for someone who may see every branch and has not picked one, otherwise the branch they work in (a branch manager, an admin, a cashier, or the director after picking a branch). _My groups_: the groups the person teaches, inside the branches they may see. Someone who has both (a branch manager who also teaches) gets a switch; a person without the Home page who teaches no group yet gets the groups their role lets them see. A teacher of one branch never gets a figure, a group or a student's name from another branch or another teacher's group. **Figures** (`src/server/services/ai/briefing.service.ts`), each shown only when the person's role may open the page behind it: Centre has payments received by method (needs `dashboard.finance`), lessons held, absences, students not marked, lessons today, new leads and leads nobody contacted, new students and students who left, debtors with the amount owed, and one line per branch when there are several. My groups has today's lessons with times, lessons held, absent students by name, students not marked by group, homework waiting to be checked, students who stopped coming (open absence cases) and the number of debtors when the role may see balances. Periods: yesterday (the default), today, the last 7 days; days are Tashkent days. (2) The model writes only the **Conclusion**, 3 to 5 short lines in the reader's language, from those same figures plus the figures of the period before for comparison; it is told to invent nothing and to treat names as data. It runs with the centre's own key from Settings → Integrations → AI assistant, low effort, no tools. (3) **Cost:** a conclusion is stored in the new `AiBriefing` table per person, view, branch, period and language, and reused for the Tashkent day while the figures are the same; when they change it is written again at most once in 30 minutes (today) or 3 hours (yesterday, 7 days). **Write the conclusion again** is honoured at most every 2 minutes, and several open tabs share one call. (4) Without a key, or when Anthropic cannot be reached, Kampus writes plain lines by its own rules (payments, attendance marked or not, leads waiting, debtors, homework waiting), translated like any label; the summary never fails because of the AI. (5) The figures come back first and the conclusion follows, so nobody waits for the model to see their numbers. (6) No new permission: the rule is "has the Home page or the Today page" (`canUseAssistant` in `src/lib/rbac/permissions.ts`), because role permissions are stored per centre and a new one would need every existing role edited by hand. (7) Money in the summary is not masked by the Home page's "Show numbers" eye; the panel is the reader's own and the old CRM shows it the same way. (8) The action log gets a line (`AI summary written`) only when the model was called. The figures sent to Anthropic include students' names for a teacher's absentees, as the assistant's lookups already do. **Tests:** `tests/unit/briefing.test.ts` (11): scope for director, branch manager and teachers of two branches, isolation, periods, keeping and rewriting, language, the fallback when Anthropic fails; `tests/e2e/assistant.spec.ts`. The frame stays put: the root and the header are excluded from the transition in `globals.css`. (2) _Home_: the cards are laid one after the other like tiles; pressing **Show numbers** rolls every figure in as a counter (`Odometer`); the greeting's words settle in turn; the setup bar fills; charts on Home and Finance draw themselves when they are scrolled to (`WhenSeen`), bars from the baseline and the donut slice by slice. (3) _Lists and forms_: rows arrive top to bottom (the first 14 staggered, the rest together, 0.6 s at most); dialogs rise with a blurred lapis scrim; menus open from their button; the tab underline grows from the middle and the tab's content rises; a switch, a tick and an attendance mark that was just pressed pop; a refused form's message shakes once; the bell rings once when something is unread; the search box widens when used. (4) _Pointer_: cards that lead somewhere lift and light the same turquoise edge as the sidebar, with a soft light under the mouse (`PointerGlow`, one listener for the page, mouse only); filled buttons get a sheen. (5) _Sign-in page_: the tiled wall is uncovered once, a band of daylight wanders over it, and the tiles under the pointer light up; the name and the form settle in. (6) _Light and dark_: the new colours open in a circle from the theme button (`document.startViewTransition` with a clip-path). **Decisions:** (a) No animation library: CSS keyframes, transforms and opacity only, plus the browser's view transitions, so phones and tablets keep their frame rate and nothing is added to what a page downloads but about 3 KB of script. (b) A counter never shows a wrong number as text: the page holds the real digits from the first frame (the rolling strip is drawn by the stylesheet with empty alternative text), so screen readers, copy and tests read the figure. (c) Everything stops under the device's **Reduce motion** setting (one block in `globals.css`, the theme circle and `PointerGlow` check it too), and printing has no animation. (d) Nothing in the interface runs longer than about 0.5 s except data being drawn and the sign-in wall; motion that is not an answer to a press exists only on the sign-in page. (e) Browsers without view transitions (older Firefox) show the new page at once; nothing depends on them. (f) The help pictures are taken with reduced motion so every page is pictured at rest. **Also fixed:** on a phone the header was wider than the screen and pushed the bell and the user menu off the edge (the branch and language buttons are icons only below 640px), and the revenue forecast card widened the page when the numbers were shown (cards may now shrink inside a grid). **Tests:** `tests/e2e/motion.spec.ts` (marker and page change, counters read as plain numbers, reduced motion, phone header). | A-193 | **A time of its own for each lesson day, and schedule changes that keep the past (added 2026-11-14 on kai's words: "work on feature where teachers can schedule same lesson in different times of different days, for example, najotbek's lesson can be 20:30 monday & 16:30 friday").** A group always could hold one slot per weekday with its own start, end and room (A-50; the switch **Different time or room per day** in the group form, with **Custom** days), and lessons, Today, the timetable, the clash check, the video links, the reminders and the student's page already read each day's own slot. What this change adds and repairs: **(1) The past stays.** Until now every edit re-planned the group from its first day, so moving a running group from Tue/Thu/Sat to Mon/Fri deleted its unmarked past lessons and invented Mondays and Fridays back to the start date, which also moved the pro-rated monthly charge (A-59) and the pay per lesson. Now `syncLessons` takes date windows: an update plans and cleans only from the day the new times start (`scheduleFrom`, today in Tashkent by default, never a later day because the timetable and the clash check read the slots the group has now) to the end date, plus any days a start date moved earlier newly covers; lessons before that day are not touched, unmarked lessons outside the group's period still go, and a day whose regular lesson is already marked keeps it and gets no second lesson at another time. The form shows **New times start from** (minimum the group's start, maximum today) only when a saved group that has started changes its days or times; an earlier day is for correcting a set-up mistake. Undoing a group day off or a branch holiday now brings back only that day instead of re-planning the whole group. Creating a group and the SOFF importer still plan the whole period. **(2) The group's own teacher may change the times** where the centre switches it on: `OrgSettings.teacherCanChangeSchedule` (Settings → General, **Teachers can change the lesson days and times of their own groups**, off by default so nothing changes for a centre until its director decides). `PATCH /groups/:id/schedule` takes only the pattern, the slots, the start day and the notice; it is open to `groups.update` and, with the switch on, to a user listed as a teacher of that group (not a support teacher, not on an archived group). A teacher cannot save over a room or teacher clash (A-116): `ignoreClashes` counts only from someone with `groups.update`. The change lands in the group's history under the teacher's name. The group page shows **Change times** next to the schedule, which opens the group form with only the days, times and rooms. **(3) The students are told**: with the box **Tell the students and parents on Telegram** ticked (default on in the form, never sent from the API unless asked), every linked chat of the group's NEW, TRIAL and ACTIVE students gets "{group}: the lesson times change from {date}. New times: Mon 20:30–22:00, Fri 16:30–18:00." in its language, and browsers that asked for notifications get the same; no auto-SMS event was added. The group's history writes a slot with its weekday's name instead of its number. `PATCH /groups/:id` no longer applies the create form's defaults to a partial body: with Zod 4 a patch that named only the group's name also reset the days to EVEN, cleared the teachers and set the status to ACTIVE (the form always sends every field, so no user was hit). **Not built:** a change that starts on a future day (make the change on that day, or give single lessons a day off with a move, A-117), two lessons on the same weekday, and a different teacher per day. Someone who holds both, where the other roles add at least one permission, has two views and a **switch in the header** whose sides carry their own role names (**Teacher** and **Branch manager**; "Full view" when there are several other roles). The choice is the nullable column `User.staffView` (TEACHING or FULL; one additive migration), so it follows the person to every device; until they choose they see everything, as before, and a one-time note under the switch says what the teacher side is. People with one side have no switch: a teacher is always in the teaching view, everyone else in the full one. `POST /api/v1/auth/view` saves the choice and is refused (403) for people with one side. **(2) The teaching view narrows the session, not only the menu.** `resolveCurrentUser` builds the actor from the roles of the view in force, so in the teaching view a teacher-manager is, for every page and every API call, a teacher: only the groups they teach (A-52), no leads, payments, finance, reports or settings, the assistant and the daily summary answer as to a teacher, and the site-owner flag is off. A view never adds a permission, it leaves some of the person's own out; the branches stay those of the account. A page the teaching view refuses says **This page is not in the teacher view** with a button that changes sides in place, instead of the plain "No access". **(3) The short menu.** In the teaching view the sidebar lists Today, Checking, Groups and Students; whatever else the person may see (Timetable, Announcements, Exams, Assistant) waits folded under **More**, which remembers being opened in that browser and opens by itself while one of its pages is in view. On a phone the same four pages are a bar along the bottom of the screen and the assistant button sits above it; the switch takes a row of its own under the header. **(4) The teacher's desk on Today.** For someone in the teaching view, today's page opens with the lesson under way or the next one on a lapis card: when it starts (a countdown, "Tomorrow", or the day), its time, group and students, and **Start video lesson** (or **Join the lesson** while a call is open; re-read every 15 s), **Students' links** and **Open the group**. Below it the day's lesson cards as before, **Homework to check** (how many answers wait and the first three, with **Check homework**), **Coming up** (the next five lessons within two weeks) and **My students** (the first eight, each with their last five marked lessons as dots). The debtors card stays only when someone owes; the "next lesson" card is the top card now. Other days, and Today for the office, are unchanged. A teacher with no group reads why and what to do (a teacher-manager: switch sides and put yourself on the group). `getTeachingDesk` reads everything through `groupScope`. **Decisions that are mine:** the switch names the person's own roles instead of "simple / full"; the default for someone who never chose is everything, because KINGSTON LC has staff with a teaching role beside another one and their first page must not change under them; teacher-only accounts in every centre get the short menu and the desk without being asked, since nothing is taken away (the rest is one press away under **More**); the teaching view narrows the API as well, so a second tab left in the other view is refused until it is reloaded. **Separation:** two branch managers still cannot see each other's branch in either view (the view only narrows; `staff-view.test` checks groups, students and the desk both ways). **Not built:** choosing the view per device, a view for roles other than teaching, and setting someone else's view for them. **On the live site this needs one thing from the people:** the teaching view shows the groups where the person is set as teacher, so each teacher-manager must be on their own group (Group → Edit → Teachers). | A-195 | **Copy the lesson link from inside the video lesson (added 2026-11-16 on kai's words: "we want teachers be able to send link to the lessons from the screen they are in during the lesson ... whether he is sharing the screen or not, then student joins the lesson, but they should login to join the lesson still").** In the lesson room a teacher (the host or any staff member in the call, never a student) has **Copy lesson link**: a button with a chain icon in the bar at the bottom beside **Leave** (with the words **Lesson link** from 1280 px), the same button under **People** above the list together with the link as text that selects itself, and, while the teacher is alone in the lesson, a line at the top that offers it. The bar is on the screen whatever is on the stage (camera pictures, a shared screen, a shown file, the whiteboard), so the button is reachable in each case; pressing it puts the link on the clipboard and shows "Lesson link copied" for eight seconds. Where the browser refuses the clipboard (plain http, an old browser) the older `execCommand` way is tried, and if that fails too the link is shown as text to select. **What the link is:** `<site>/student/lesson/<groupId>`, with no language in it (the visitor's own language is chosen on arrival) and built from the address the teacher is on, so a centre on its own domain (A-114) hands out its own address. It names the group and nothing else: it is the same for every lesson, can be pinned in the group's Telegram chat, never has to be reset, and is no credential. **Opening it:** without a student session the visitor is sent to `/student/login?next=/student/lesson/<groupId>` and sees nothing of the group, not even whether it exists; the sign-in page says "Sign in to join your lesson". After Telegram sign-in (A-150; `safeNext` already accepts the path) the page looks for a current membership (New, Trial or Active, student and group not archived) of the group among the students behind the account, the person's own record first, then a child's, and redirects to that membership's personal page `/class/<token>`, where the existing lobby checks camera and microphone and **Join lesson** enters the call (the page waits by itself when the lesson has not started). A membership that never had a personal link gets one at that moment. A signed-in student or parent who is not in the group stays on a card "This lesson is for another group" with a button to their own groups; nothing about the group is shown. A signed-in staff member who may see the group (the teacher pressing their own link, a colleague) goes to the running call `/video/<roomId>`, or to the group's page when no lesson is on; staff without access to the group are treated like any visitor. Sign-in from the bot (`/start login`) does not carry the lesson through: the student lands on My Kampus, where the group shows **Join** while the lesson is on, and the sign-in page says so. **Decisions that are mine:** one link per group instead of one per lesson, so it can be sent once and kept; the link leads to the student's existing personal page instead of a second way into the call, so attendance from the call, the lesson panel and everything else work unchanged; staff other than the host may copy it too; the students' personal links (A-100, `/class/<token>`) are left as they are and still open without signing in, because they are already out by SMS and Telegram and each belongs to one student. **Open for kai:** whether personal links should also ask for a sign-in before joining a lesson. **Not built:** carrying the lesson through a bot sign-in, sending the link from Kampus to the group's Telegram chat, a QR code of the link. No migration, no new permission, no setting. | A-196 | **Sign-in with a Telegram code, a waiting list, and passwords after the first sign-in (added 2026-11-16 on kai's words: "it will be easier if we setup telegram login where you recieve a code from telegram to login instead of having to sign in and authorize with telegram app ... first time when they login to the platform from anywhere, they have to do it from telegram, if someone logs in before their phone number is added to the database, they should be in a wait list or smth like that so that teacher or manager can approve them. after first login, they can setup their password. then by default their login will be phone number + password, with option to login from telegram without password. that described login process works for everyone, teachers & students ... we need to add instructions on how to login from telegram in login page as well").** **(1) How the code travels, and why this way.** The code is sent by the centre's own Kampus bot (or the server's shared bot, A-135), not by Telegram Gateway. Gateway sends a code to any phone number without the person doing anything first, but it is a paid service (about one US cent per code at the time of writing, from a prepaid balance on a separate Telegram account that someone has to open, verify and top up), and it cannot be tried without that account. The bot is free, is already set up and already receives its webhook on the live site, and needs no new keys. Its one limit is that a bot may not write to someone who has never opened it, and does not know anybody's phone number. So the person shares their own number with the bot once: the sign-in page links to `https://t.me/<bot>?start=login`, the bot answers with a **Share my number** button, and Telegram delivers the contact. A contact whose `user_id` is the sender's own is that person's verified number; anything else is refused ("share your own number"). The pair is kept in `TelegramContact` (bot's centre + Telegram user, chat, phone); a phone belongs to one Telegram account at a time. **(2) The steps.** On either sign-in page the person types their phone and presses **Get a code in Telegram** (`POST /auth/code`). The answer is the same for every phone, known or not, so the page cannot be used to look people up. If the bot knows the phone, the code goes to that chat at once; if not, it is sent the moment the person shares their number (`pendingCodeFor`), so a first-timer does both steps in either order. The code is six digits, valid for 10 minutes, usable once, stored only as a hash (`PhoneSignInCode`), with five tries per code; wrong codes count toward the same lock as wrong passwords (five in 15 minutes lock the phone), one phone gets at most five codes and one address thirty in 15 minutes. `POST /auth/code/verify` then decides by the phone: a staff member gets a staff session (marked as a Telegram sign-in), a student or parent a student session, anyone else the waiting list. The page the person started on only decides which is tried first, so a teacher who opens the student page still lands in the staff app. On a centre's own domain only that centre's people come in; on the server's address the shared bot serves everyone, else the only centre with a bot, else the site owner's centre. **(3) First sign-in is with Telegram.** `User.telegramVerifiedAt` records that Telegram has proven the person's phone (a code, or the older Telegram page). Until it is set, a staff password opens nothing, even the right one: the page answers "Your first sign-in is with Telegram" (only after a correct password, so it says nothing about other people's phones). The migration fills the column for everyone who has already signed in with Telegram, so nobody on the live site has to do anything new. The rule holds only where a bot with a real token serves the centre, so a fresh server or a centre without a bot still opens with passwords, and `STAFF_PASSWORD_LOGIN=on` lifts it in an emergency. Students and parents never had passwords, so for them the first sign-in is by Telegram by construction. **(4) A password afterwards.** Right after a Telegram sign-in someone without a password of their own is taken to **Choose a password** once (`passwordOfferedAt`); **Not now** skips it, and My account (staff) or the student home offers it again. In a session Telegram opened, setting a password does not ask for the old one (`POST /auth/set-password`, `POST /student-auth/password`), which is also the way back after a forgotten password; in a password session the current password is asked for. Students and parents get `StudentAccount.passwordHash`; a student password opens only the records of the centre whose address is used. Staff added by a manager need no password any more: the form may leave it empty, and a password a manager does set stays temporary as before (A-124). The second step after a password (A-124) is unchanged. **(5) The waiting list.** A proven phone that no staff member, student or parent has is not turned away. The page asks for the person's name, the centre (when the address serves several), the branch and an optional note, and the request (`JoinRequest`) goes to the staff of that branch who may add students, or staff when it was made on the staff page: a notification, and a line at the top of Students or Settings → Staff that opens **Sign-in requests** (`/join-requests`). **Let in** offers: a new student (branch and optional group), an existing student (the phone goes on their card), a parent of a student, or, for a staff request, a new staff member with a role. Each goes through the service that normally does it, so the same rights and branch limits hold; teachers see student requests when **Teachers can add students** is on. **Decline** keeps the request under the Declined tab, where it can still be approved. A request also closes by itself when the phone is added anywhere else in Kampus. The bot tells the person either way, with the link to sign in. Nothing of the centre is shown to someone who waits. **(6) Instructions.** Both sign-in pages carry the four steps under the button, with the bot's name and a link that opens it; the code step repeats what to do when no message came. The in-app help has the same steps for staff and for students, and a section on Sign-in requests. **(7) What went away, and what stayed.** The switches **Staff sign in with Telegram only** (A-180) and **Every centre on this server signs in with Telegram only** (A-181) are removed with their checks; their two columns stay in the database, unused, so the migration only adds. The older sign-in on Telegram's own page (A-150, A-180) still works where its keys are saved, as a small link under the form, and also counts as the first Telegram sign-in. **Test servers:** with `TELEGRAM_LOGIN_FAKE=1` a bot without a token counts as able to send, delivers into the test outbox, and a code is the last six digits of the phone; that switch must never be set on a live server. Covered by `sign-in-codes.test`, `staff-telegram-login.test`, `sign-in-codes.spec`. **Risk: high.** A phone number proven by Telegram opens the account, as it already did (A-150, A-180); what is new is that a password chosen by the person does too, so a weak or shared password is now a way in. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and attempts are rate-limited. The waiting list relies on staff judging who a stranger is: Kampus proves the phone, not the identity. If the bot is blocked by a person or its token is revoked, codes stop; the older Telegram page, an existing password and `STAFF_PASSWORD_LOGIN=on` remain. | A-197 | **How-to videos, one per feature, in English, Russian and Uzbek (added 2026-11-17 on kai's words: "work on creating video in english, russian and uzbek on how to use everything, starting from creating accounts till setting up lessons and the rest" and "make each video seperate for each feature").** There are 23 videos per language, each about one to two minutes: signing in, finding your way around, the home page, adding staff, sign-in requests, courses and rooms, opening a group, the timetable and moving a lesson, adding a student, leads and trial lessons, payments and debtors, the teacher's day (attendance and grades), video lessons, homework and checking, materials with the stream and the group chat, exams, tests and coins, announcements, finance with payroll and the cash desk, reports, the student's page, integrations, and the AI assistant. **What a video is:** 1920×1080, 30 frames a second, H.264 with a silent sound track (so messengers treat it as a video, not a GIF). | A-200 | **Screen sharing made dependable (added 2026-11-22 on kai's words: "why in google meet everything works but in our app sometimes screenshare doesn't work? we have to find a fix for that").** **What was checked:** nine share cases were run between two real browsers (teacher or student sharing, with a camera, without one, with it off, a Full HD screen and a 2880×1800 one) and the picture arrived in all of them, so the connection itself was not at fault. Reading the code and measuring found five faults that each look like "it does not work" to a person. **(1) Silence on failure:** every error of the browser's screen request was swallowed, so a refused request left a button that did nothing. Now the reason is sorted (`shareFailure` in `call-engine.ts`): the person closed the picker (no error), the browser or computer refused ("blocked": Chrome's "denied by system", or a refusal faster than any picker could be shown), the window or screen could not be captured ("unreadable"), anything else ("failed"). The room shows the reason with the Mac permission path and **Try again**. A browser that rejects the options is asked once more with the plainest request. **(2) The screen was hidden:** the whiteboard, a shown file, the teacher's spotlight and a viewer's earlier pin all went before a shared screen, so students kept seeing the old thing and the screen sat in a thumbnail. Now a teacher's share closes the whiteboard and the shown file (the newest choice wins), a share goes before the spotlight, a new share clears a viewer's pin, and whoever shares under an open whiteboard or file is told so (**Show my screen** for the teacher). **(3) Size and budget:** the screen was captured at its full size (a Retina display is five megapixels) and sent under the camera's budget, 600-900 kbit/s for a teacher and 120-400 for a student, with one encoder per receiver. Measured for one receiver at 2880×1800: 30 ms of processor per picture. Now the capture is asked for at 1920×1080 at most and a share has its own budget whoever shares (`screenSending`): 1.5 Mbit/s at 1080 lines for up to 3 receivers, 1.0 at 900 for up to 6, 0.7 at 720 above, at most 15 pictures a second; measured 17 ms per picture for the same screen. **(4) Echo:** the picker offered the lesson's own tab and the computer's whole sound, both of which send everyone's voice back to them. Now the own tab is excluded and system sound is asked for only where the browser can leave the tab's own sound out (`restrictOwnAudio`), else only a shared tab's sound. **(5) Safari's own preview** kept the old picture when the track changed under it; the tile now sets the stream again. **A log line per failure:** the browser reports a failed or partly failed share with its next poll (`issue` in the sync body) and the server writes `[video] share <reason>: <error> (room, role, browser)`, so the next "sometimes" has a reason (`docker compose logs app \| grep '\[video\]'`). **What stays as it is:** Kampus sends video straight from browser to browser, so a sharer uploads one copy per person, where Google Meet uploads one copy to its servers; in a full room of 12 that is about 8 Mbit/s of upload, and a slow line shows as a slow picture. A media server (LiveKit or similar) would remove that limit and is a separate decision. Phones and tablets still cannot share a screen: no Android browser offers screen capture to a web page, whichever version (kai met this on a Galaxy Z Fold with an up-to-date Chrome; Google Meet can there because it is an installed app), and Apple allows it only from iPadOS and iOS 27 (A-182). The notice now says so in words that fit the device, and **Show a file to everyone** (A-183) is the way there; sharing a phone's screen would need an installed Kampus app. No migration, no setting. Not tried on the live site or in Safari. | A-202 | **The server can move to a new address, and the old one keeps leading to it (added 2026-11-22 on kai's words: "check for domains for our app, we have to buy one", then "let's go with kampus.center" and "domain is purchased, go ahead with configuration").** Kampus ran under the free name `2-31-30-140.sslip.io`; kai bought `kampus.center` at Cloudflare. **What a person sees:** the site opens at `https://kampus.center`. A page opened under the old name (a saved bookmark, a lesson link sent last week, a receipt link) answers with a redirect to the same page under the new name. Everyone signs in once more, because a browser keeps the sign-in per address; phone and password work as before. Links Kampus sends from now on carry the new address. **How it works:** `.env` gets `DOMAIN` and `APP_URL` for the new name and one new optional line, `FORMER_DOMAIN`, with the old name (several names separated by a comma and a space; `www.kampus.center` is listed there too, so it leads to the address without `www`). `docker/Caddyfile` has a second site for those names: every path outside `/api` is redirected to `https://<DOMAIN><same path>` (302, not permanent, so nothing is cached for good if the address ever changes again), and `/api` is passed to the app as before. **Why `/api` stays under the old name:** Telegram, Payme and Click call the address they were given and do not follow a redirect, so a webhook registered under the old name would silently stop; this way the bot's webhook keeps arriving until it is moved, and nothing has to happen in the same minute as the switch. **Without `FORMER_DOMAIN`** the block is a plain-http site for a name nobody can reach (`former-address.invalid`), so Caddy asks for no certificate and a server that never moved behaves as before. **Decisions (DEFAULT):** the old name is kept for as long as old links may be around, it costs nothing; the DNS record at Cloudflare is DNS only (not proxied), because Caddy fetches its own certificate and the video relay (TURN) needs a direct line to the server; the app itself is not changed and does not know about former names, the redirect lives in the proxy alone; a centre's own address (A-114) is not touched. **Still by hand after the switch** (`docs/DEPLOY.md` section 13): the older sign-in on Telegram's own page needs the new Redirect URI and Trusted Origin in BotFather (A-179), sign-in with a code from the bot (A-196) is not affected; the bot's webhook and any Payme or Click callback address move to the new name when convenient. No page of the app changes, so the in-app help has nothing to add. **Checked:** CI runs `caddy validate` on `docker/Caddyfile` with and without `FORMER_DOMAIN`, with one name and with two; the update line validates the configuration on the server with the server's own Caddy before anything restarts.
