| A-230 | **Every site feature in the app, part 1: the centre's home, the bell, search, the menu and "My salary" (added 2026-11-23, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** The site's pages are brought into the app part by part; this is the first of six. **Who gets it:** the office, that is the full view with the right to the dashboard (`dashboard.view`). They start at **Home** and their bar is Home, Today, Groups, Students, More (a tablet's rail has room for Checking too; on a phone Checking is in the menu under More). Teachers and the teaching view keep Today, Groups, Checking, Students, More and start at Today. **Home** is the site's home page made for a phone: the welcome line, **Show numbers** (every figure and sum is `***` until it is pressed, as on the site), the centre's utilisation, a branch filter for people with several branches; the setup checklist (what is left to do as rows that open their page, what is done named in one line, **Hide**); the twelve figures as tiles, two in a row on a phone and four on a tablet, each opening the page the site opens; the revenue forecast (this month collected against expected, next month, six months as bars, the split by course and by branch); the room schedule of a weekday as a list per room (the site's grid of rooms against hours does not fit a phone), a lesson opening its group; the money: a year with arrows, a month, a payment type, the four sums, income by payment type, and the year by months as bars of income and expenses. A part is asked for only if the person may see it: the money and forecast need `dashboard.finance`, the checklist `settings.org`. **Charts:** two sums per step of time, one scale, lapis and turquoise (checked for colour-blind readers in light and dark), a legend, and the pressed step's sums written under the plot since a phone has no hover. **The bell and the search** stand at the right of Home's header and as the first rows of the menu, for every staff member: notifications newest first, all or unread, a press marks one read and opens what it is about, **Mark all as read**; the search finds students, groups and leads from two letters on. **The menu** under More is the site's navigation as one list of the pages the person's rights open, plus Notifications, Search and "My salary" (for people who are paid). A row with an arrow out opens on the site, already signed in (A-204); the others open in the app. **Where a page opens:** `nativeRoute` in `mobile/src/features/office/site-paths.ts` knows which site paths the app has (a student, a group, Home, Today, Checking, Groups, Students, Announcements, Notifications, Search, My salary); a filtered list such as "debtors" opens on the site until the app can filter the same way, so a figure never leads to an unfiltered list. **My salary** shows a month with arrows, its state with the accountant, the four sums, the rule, the groups with their share, bonuses, fines and advances, and earlier months. **Decided:** the app has no payment-type list of its own, it offers the types that took money in the chosen period; the years go back with an arrow instead of a list. **Not in this part:** the other pages of the menu (students for the office and payments, leads and calls, groups and timetable management, finance and reports, settings and the assistant) are parts 2 to 6 and open on the site until then. Nothing changes on the server: the app uses the calls the site already makes. | A-231 | **Every site feature in the app, part 2: students for the office (added 2026-11-23, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Second of six parts (A-230 was the first). **The list:** people in the full view get a **Filters** button on Students: payment status (due soon, debtor, not a debtor, overpaid), status in the group (active, new, frozen, left after trial, without a group), course, group (narrowed by the course), teacher, and "Archived students only". Nothing changes until **Show**; the button then reads "Filters: 2" and **Clear** stands beside it. The home page's figures about students ("Remaining debt", "Payment due soon", "Active students", "New group admissions", "Left this month" without the right to reports) now open this list with the filter set, where part 1 sent them to the site; `nativeRoute` passes the filters and values it knows and still sends any other address to the site ("In trial lessons" among them: its address carries a status the list's filter does not have). Teachers (the teaching view) keep the plain list. **Add student** (right `students.create`): a sheet with the branch (when the person has several), full name, phone, day of birth, gender, a group to join with the day of joining, a parent's phone and name, a note. The server's own checks apply (the phone format, the group's branch, who may create) and its messages are shown under the fields; the new student's page opens when it is saved. The rest of the site's form (school, source, the app password, "invited by", the time zone, a price of their own in the group) stays on the site for now. **Make a payment** (right `payments.create`, not for an archived student) on the student's page is the site's Payment dialog: the group, its balance and monthly price, the sum with **Fill in** (the server's suggestion: the debt, or a month's price), the payment method, the month it is for (the server's list, the suggested one chosen), the day, a comment. Saved, the balances, the lists and the home page's figures are asked for again. Bonus sums, refunds, receipts and balance corrections stay on the site for now. **Edit, Archive, Restore** on the student's page: **Edit** (right `students.update`) changes the name, phone, day of birth and note; **Archive** (right `students.delete`) asks first, with the site's words that the student leaves every group; an archived student has **Restore** instead. **Payments** is a new part of the student's page for the full view: each payment with its day, group, month, method, who took it, and what was refunded from it, and the total. **Dates** are typed as day.month.year (`DateField`; the dots appear by themselves), since that is how they are written here; the phone's own date wheel was left out to keep one behaviour on iPhone, Android and the browser build. **Also here:** the video recorder films the phone app with Playwright's headless shell, because a Chromium window on a Mac cannot be narrower than 500 px and the first voiced recording on the Mac failed on it (DEPLOY.md section 12). Nothing changes on the server. | A-232 | **Every site feature in the app, part 3: leads and the people to call (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Third of six parts. **The board** (`/staff/leads`): the site's board with its board picker, a search, the owner filter and the archive switch. A phone shows one column at a time, the columns being the chips above it with their counts; a tablet shows the columns side by side. Dragging is not offered: a lead moves by **Move to** on its card, because dragging across a scrolling phone screen moves things by accident. **A lead's card** is one sheet with the numbers to dial, what is known, and a button for each thing the person may do: Log a contact (channel, outcome, note, next contact, status: the site's dialog), Book a trial (groups of the lead's branch only), History (trials, with Cancel on a booked one, then contacts), Edit, Add to a group, Add to waiting list, Student profile, Archive (asks first) or Restore, Delete (asks first). Each button follows the site's permission (`leads.update`, `leads.create`, `leads.delete`). A new lead goes into the column whose **Add lead** was pressed and is owned by whoever adds it, as on the site; who invited the lead is shown but set on the site. **Calls today** (`/staff/leads/calls`): the four counts, the range and owner filters (the person's own due leads first), a press opens the lead's card. **Waiting list** (`/staff/leads/waitlist`): filters, add and edit, Enrol in a group of the entry's course and branch, Declined, Back to waiting, Remove (asks first); offering a new group's seats stays on the group's page of the site. **Inbox** (`/staff/leads/inbox`): open, closed or all chats with the unread count, a chat as a thread with a reply box (sent through the centre's bot), Open lead, Close or Reopen. **Sign-in requests** (`/staff/join-requests`): a row of the app's menu with the number waiting, shown to whoever may add students or staff (on the site it is a banner); Let in as a new student, an existing student, a parent, or a new member of staff with a role; Decline asks first. **Absences** (`/staff/absences`): the four counts, the filters, each case with why it is on the list and the last contact, Log a contact (the student's and the parent's number dial with one press), History, and links to the student and the group. A notification or a search result about a lead opens the board with the name searched. **Not in the app yet, on the site:** making and renaming boards and columns, the sources report, ticking several leads at once (bulk move, archive, SMS, add to group), the Excel exports, SMS to a column, the visitor's trial link, and the absence rules. Nothing changes on the server: the app makes the calls the site's pages make. | A-233 | **Every site feature in the app, part 4a: groups for the office and the timetable (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fourth of six parts, first half. **The Groups tab**: in the full view, someone with `groups.view` gets every group they may see by name, 30 at a time, with the site's four filters (status, course, teacher, days), a search by name, and **New group** for `groups.create`; in the teaching view a teacher keeps the short cards of their own groups. **The group form** (`GroupFormSheet`) is the site's drawer with its rules: branch (a new group, when the person has more than one), name, course of that branch, grading system, billing (monthly or packages, A-178), days (even, odd, every day, or chosen weekdays), one time and room for every lesson day or a time and room per day (A-193), up to three teachers of that branch with role and share, start and end date, and the status of an existing group. An existing group whose days or times change is asked from which day the new times count (only when it has already started) and whether the students and parents are told (A-193). A room or teacher that is already busy comes back as a list ("Tue 09:00–10:30: room 101 is taken by …"); the button then reads **Save anyway** and resends the very same form with `ignoreClashes` (A-116); any change to the form hides the warning again. **A group's page** has a card for the office: course, price or "Lesson packages", branch (when there is more than one), dates, lessons held, the teachers with their role (and their share, for `groups.update` only), support teachers and the days off, where a day a student moved or cancelled themselves is worded, not shown as its key. Buttons: **Edit**, **Change times** and **More** (support teachers, change teacher, give a day off with an optional move of the lesson, move to another branch when the person has more than one, finish, archive for `groups.delete`); a day off can be taken back. The group's own teacher sees only **Change times**, and only where the centre has switched that on (A-193). An archived group offers nothing. **Manage students** (`groups.update`) opens the group's students with status, balance, lessons left in a package and the reason someone left: a search, **Removed**, **Activate students**, **Add student** (one the centre has, found by name or phone, or a new student for `students.create`, with the join day, the charged-from day (A-110), a custom price and a note), and for one student: the allowed status moves (A-08), a payment (`payments.create`, the app's Payment sheet), move to another group, the charged-from day, their page, and remove with one of the centre's reasons or free words (A-92). **A student's page** has **Add to a group** (`groups.update`), which is also how a restored student gets back into a group. **Timetable** (`/staff/timetable`, in the More menu): by room or by teacher, the branch when there are several; a phone shows one weekday at a time, a tablet the seven days side by side; a lesson opens its group. **On the server** two read-only calls were added, because the site reads these lists on its pages and the app has to ask for them: `GET /api/v1/groups/options` (courses, rooms, grading systems and teachers of the person's branches, and whether teachers may change times; `groups.view`) and `GET /api/v1/groups/timetable?mode&branchId&id` (`groups.view`). The site itself is unchanged; an older server answers "Not found" to the two calls. **Also fixed, from the Android run of parts 1 and 2:** a sheet with the keyboard open no longer slides under the status bar or loses its title and Save button (it gives up height instead, on a phone and on a tablet on its side); a sheet on Android is a solid pane (the list behind showed between the fields); a tap just under a header button goes to the page, not to Search. **Left on the site for now:** a group's packages and discounts, offering seats to the waiting list, the Excel import and exports, SMS to a group, return to leads, extra lessons. | A-234 | **Every site feature in the app, part 4b: teachers, courses, rooms and the Settings list (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fourth of six parts, second half; exams follow as A-235. **Teachers** (`/staff/teachers`, the More menu's Teachers row, `teachers.view`): two lists as on the site, teachers and support teachers, each with a search by name or phone and its archive, 30 at a time; a teacher's row says how they are paid, a support teacher's row the groups they help in. **New teacher** (`teachers.create`) adds to the list in view, which fixes the role as on the site. **The form** (`TeacherFormSheet`) has the site's fields: full name, phone, date of birth, hire date, branches (when there is more than one), the way of paying (percent, monthly, per lesson, per student) with its sum, and gender. It has **no photo and no password field**: the first sign-in is with a code from Telegram and the person chooses their own password (A-196), and nobody types one for them in the app. For an existing teacher the form also has **Account safety**: "Ask for a Telegram code at sign-in" (only for someone the bot can reach, A-124) and **Sign out of all devices**. Changing the way of paying keeps the sums of the other ways, as the site's form does. **A teacher's page** (`/staff/teachers/[id]`): roles, phone, registered, branches, the pay line, hire date and birthday, the three counts (courses taught, active groups, active students), the groups they teach or support (each opens the group's page), **Edit** (`teachers.update`) and **Archive** after a question (`teachers.delete`, never yourself). An archived teacher is only read, as on the site, which has no way to bring one back either. **Hours open for 1:1 booking** (A-169): the week on a card, and **Change hours** with a sheet of windows per weekday (up to 21, an end after its start); the office changes them on a teacher's page with `teachers.update`, and a teacher finds their own card under **More**, as on the site's "My account". **Settings** (`/staff/settings`, the More menu's Settings row): the site's sections in its order, each behind the same permission; **Courses** and **Rooms** open in the app and every other section opens on the site, already signed in, with the arrow that says so. "Organisations" is the site owner's page and stays on the site (the app is not told who the site owner is). A test on the site's side fails when the two lists part ways. **Courses** (`settings.catalog`): each course with its colour, notes, monthly price, length, branch and grading system; a press offers **Edit**, **Syllabus** and **Archive**; the archive is a list of its own and is only read. The form has the branch (a new course, when there is more than one), name, notes, price, months (1 to 60), grading system, one of ten colours (a colour set on the site that is not among them stays a choice), and the five grade weights, which must add up to 100 (A-162). The syllabus is one topic a line, saved as a whole (A-137). **Rooms** (`settings.catalog`): name, branch and seats; add, change, delete after a question. **On the server** nothing was added for these pages: they use the calls the site's pages make. **Fixed, from the iPhone and iPad run of parts 1 and 2:** on Home, a payment type chosen for the year stayed in force after choosing a month that has no such payments, with its list gone and the sums filtered unseen (the choice now counts only while the period shown has that type); "Income by payment method" now ends with **Other income** when there is some, so the card adds up to Income; two long sums in "This month" no longer run over the card on a tablet held upright; a sheet is a denser pane of glass, so a bright button behind it does not glow through between the fields, and its dim covers the whole window also with a hardware keyboard attached; opening a list from a form puts the keyboard away first, so an iPhone does not bring it back over the form; the tablet's side rail starts under the status bar, so the clock is readable in light mode; the chips on a student's page wrap, so **Payments** is not off the screen; the bell's unread list says "No unread notifications." when it is empty. **One change on the site:** a page opened from the phone app (A-204) arrives with a half-hour cookie, `kampus_from_app`, and the day's summary (A-190) does not open over it by itself; the button in the corner still opens it. **Left on the site for now:** a teacher's photo, the Excel file and SMS to teachers, the Excel import of courses and rooms, and every other Settings section. | A-235 | **Every site feature in the app, part 4c: exams (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fourth of six parts, last third. **Exams** (`/staff/exams`, the More menu's and Home's Exams, `exams.view`): the site's Exams page. Two lists, **Group exams** and **Mock exams**, each with its count under the filters in force; the filters are the site's: status (what is not started first, as on the site), group, from and to. A card says the exam's name, day and time, group or groups, examiner, room, the pass score out of the maximum, and how many students it has (a mock exam: registrations out of its seats, and its price). A centre that hides the exam schedule from teachers (Settings → General) gets the same sentence the site shows. **Add exam** (`exams.create`) opens the site's form (`ExamFormSheet`): the kind (a group's exam or a mock exam; fixed once the exam exists), the name, then for a group's exam its group and **Retake**, and for a mock exam the price, the groups it is for and the seats. The groups of a mock exam are narrowed down as on the site, by course, by months studied and by branch, and **Filter and select all** ticks what is left; single groups are ticked by hand. Then the day, start and end (an end after its start), **Additional details** with an examiner and a room (only rooms of the group's branch are offered), the grading system or **Custom**, and the pass and maximum scores (a pass score no higher than the maximum; "7,5" and "7.5" are both read). **An exam's page** (`/staff/exam/[id]`; the site's `/exams/:id` opens it): kind, status, retake, branch, the facts above, and with `exams.update` **Edit**, **Finish** or **Reopen**; with `exams.delete` **Delete** after a question, offered only while nobody has a score, as on the site. **The grading sheet**: every student of the group (a mock exam: everyone registered) with **Present**, a score and a comment; **Passed**, **Failed**, **Not graded** or **Absent** shows as the score is typed; **Save results** sends the whole sheet in one call, as the site does, and is only active when something was changed. A score that is not a number, or above the exam's maximum, is marked under its field and nothing is sent. Whoever may only look (`exams.view`) sees the scores, levels and comments without fields. **A mock exam's registrations** (`exams.update`): a search by name or phone (two letters at least) lists students of the exam's groups who are not registered yet, a press registers one, and when the seats are taken the search gives way to "Capacity reached."; **Remove registration** on a row asks first (the site removes at once; on a phone a slip of the finger is easier, and a registration takes its score with it). **On a group's Exams page** (A-219) there is now **Add exam** for whoever may add one, with the group given, and **Open the exam** on each card, which is how a teacher who may grade reaches the sheet; the sentence "Exams are set up and graded on the site" is gone. **On the server** nothing was added: the app uses the calls the site's pages make (`/exams`, `/exams/options`, `/exams/:id`, `/finish`, `/reopen`, `/results`, `/registrations`, `/candidates`), so saving a score sends the exam-result SMS exactly as it does from the site (A-88). **Also in this change:** the site's test that keeps the app's Settings list equal to the site's now reads the app's file as text, because the site's test run does not have the app's packages. | A-236 | **Every site feature in the app, part 5a: debts and the cash desk (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fifth of six parts, first half. **Debtors** (`/staff/debts`, the More menu's and Home's Debtors, `payments.create` as on the site): the site's Debtors page (A-112). On top the four figures (debtors, owed in total, promised to pay, need a call). Under them a search by name or phone, the site's **Show** filter (open and promised by default, open, promised, need a call, closed, all), an order (the site's sortable columns, each in its useful direction: longest overdue first by default, most owed, nearest promise, longest without contact, name) and, for someone who sees several branches and chose none at the top, the branch. A card says the student, what they owe, **Promised**, **Call** or why the case was closed, the phone (it dials), the groups that are short, for how many days and since when, the promise with its day and sum (red and "missed" once the day has passed), how many promises were missed, the last contact with how, what came of it and who, and whether a Telegram message or an SMS was sent. Thirty debtors at a time, **Show more** for the next. A press on a card offers what the site's row menu offers: **Call and log the outcome** and **Log a contact** (the same sheet, starting on Call or on Note: how, the outcome, and for **Promised to pay** the day, which is required, and an optional sum; the student's and the parent's numbers dial from the sheet), **Send a Telegram reminder** (the answer says to how many chats it went, or that the student has no Telegram chat connected), **History** (every contact, newest first, with what the server wrote on its own marked "automatic") and **Open the student** (only with `students.view`). A closed case keeps its history and the student's page only. A notification's address (`/debts?status=NEEDS_CALL&branchId=…`, `/debts?status=OPEN&q=…`) opens the app's list with that filter; a filter the list does not know stays the site's. The Excel file stays on the site. **Cash desk** (`/staff/cashdesk`, the More menu, `payments.create` or `finance.view` as on the site): the site's Cash desk page (A-122). The day closes of a year and a month (this month by default, **Whole year**; next year and three years back, as on the site) and of a branch for someone who chose none, with the totals (expected cash, counted cash, difference, how many await the hand-over) and a card per close: the day, the branch, the cashier (only for `finance.view`, as the site's column), what was received in how many payments, expected and counted cash, the difference with its sign (short in red, over in green), the note, and **Awaiting hand-over** or **Accepted by** with the name. **Accept** (`finance.update`) is on a close not yet accepted. **Print** opens the site's sheet for that close (`/cashdesk/:id`), signed in, because printing is the browser's. **Close the day** (`payments.create`): the branch (when the person has several), the day (today by default; a day in the future is refused in the form and nothing is asked), then what the server counts for that cashier, branch and day: each payment type with its net and, under it, payments, refunds, expenses and other income, the types marked as cash named so, the number of payments with what was received, and the expected cash. The cashier enters the counted cash (required; zero is a figure) and sees the difference at once, and may add a note. The figures are asked for again every time the sheet opens and whenever the branch or the day changes, never taken from an earlier look. Three notices as on the site: no payment type is marked as cash; the day was closed before and not accepted, so saving replaces that close; the day was closed and accepted, and then the fields and the button are off. **On the server** nothing was added: the app uses the calls the site's pages make (`/debts`, `/debts/:id/contacts`, `/debts/:id/remind`, `/cashdesk`, `/cashdesk/preview`, `/cashdesk/:id/accept`). | A-237 | **Every site feature in the app, part 5b: finance and payroll (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fifth of six parts, second of three. **Finance** (`/staff/finance`, the More menu's Finance and Home's money cards, `finance.view`): the site's Finance page. Filters: year (next year and three back, as on the site), month or **Whole year** (the default), payment type, and the branch for someone who sees several and chose none at the top. **Key figures**: income, expenses, profit, active balance (it opens Investments, as on the site), LTV, CAC, marketing efficiency and average payment. **Income by payment method** is a row per type with a bar to scale (the site draws a ring; a phone reads rows better) and **the year's turnover** is the paired bars of Home (A-230), a press on a month writing its two sums. **Plan for the month** (the chosen month, or this month while a whole year is shown): achieved with the percent done, expected with the percent left, the progress bar, the monthly plan, the active debt with the number of debtors, prepayments and the month's share; **Effect time** switches between counting a payment in the month it is for and in the month it was paid, as on the site. **Expense report** and **Income report**: a card per category with the period's sum, on the expense side also Advances and Marketing; the site's addresses open them): the period's total, the filters the site has there (year, month, payment type except for investments, staff member for the kinds that name one), and a card per entry with who it was for (a staff member, a student, or an investor's name), the sum, the day, the payment type, the comment and, for expenses and income, who wrote it. **The add button** carries the site's words for the kind ("Give bonus", "Add expense"); it opens the site's one form (`EntrySheet`): branch (when the centre has several), payment type (may be left unset; not for an investment), the category when the page is not a category's own, for an expense or income **Staff member / Student** with the staff list or a search of students by name or phone (two letters at least, only students of the entry's branch), for an advance, bonus or fine the staff member (required), for an investment the investor's full name (required), the sum (above zero; "1 500 000" and "1500,5" are both read, parts of a soʻm as on the site), the day and a comment. A press on an entry offers **Edit** (`finance.update`) and **Delete** (`finance.delete`, after a question). A bonus, a fine or an advance changes the month's payroll, so the app asks for the payroll again after one is saved or deleted. **A month's payroll** (`/staff/finance/salary/[month]`; the site's `/finance/salary-detail/2026-11-01` opens it; the server computes a month the first time it is asked for): the staff and approved counts, **Draft** or **Saved**, the totals by part (fixed, percent, lessons, students, bonus, fines with their count, advance) and the sum of salaries; a search by name; a card per staff member with the role (a system role in the reader's language, a centre's own as typed), the salary (red with a warning sign when negative), and on a press what it is made of and from which groups ("20% × UZS 500,000 × 12 students"). **Approve** on a line needs `finance.payroll.approve`; an approved line names who approved it. **Recalculate** (it leaves approved lines as they are, as on the site), **Save draft** and **Save** need `finance.update` and stay at the bottom of the screen. **Excel file on the site** opens the site's page of that month, signed in, because the file is the browser's to download. **On the server** one read-only call was added for the app: `GET /api/v1/finance/totals?branchId&year&month` (`finance.view`) answers what the site's page reads on the server itself, the period's entries added up by type and the number of cashier day closes with how many await the hand-over. | A-238 | **Every site feature in the app, part 5c: reports (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** Fifth of six parts, third of four (the last three reports are part 5d). **Reports** (`/staff/reports`, the More menu's Reports, `reports.view`, `reports.payments` or `reports.leads`): the site's list in its order, only the reports the person has the right to. A report the app has carries an arrow; Graduates, Staff attendance and Coins carry the sign of a page that opens on the site, signed in. Home's **Left this month** and **Center utilisation** now open the app's reports. **Every report** starts with the site's row of filters: the branch (for someone who sees several and chose none at the top), the year (next year and three back) and the month, this month at first. A filter of a row of filters has no label above it, so with nothing chosen it says what it filters by ("Group", "Teacher") in the grey of a hint, and its list starts with **All**. Key figures are cards, two to a row on a phone and three or four on a tablet, with the percent against the month before in green or red where the site shows one. A table of the site is a card per row with its numbers under small names, two cards to a row on a tablet. **Excel file on the site** at the end of each report opens the same report on the site with the same filters, because the file is the browser's to download. **Payments** (`reports.payments`): total, on time, late, discounts, bonus and refunds with their counts, then **By teachers** (groups, students, total, debt in red) or **By staff** (payments, total, refunds). **Student payments** (`reports.payments`): the count and the sum, **By payment date** (the month the money came in, not the month paid for), a search by name or phone, and the site's six filters (group, payment method, teacher, course, with or without bonus, received by); a card per payment with the sum, a refund in red under it, the group and teacher, the day, the month paid for, the payment type, the bonus, who took it and the comment; 30 at a time with **Show more**; a card opens the student for someone with `students.view`. **Left students** (`reports.view`): From and To (this month at first; half a date is not asked for, and a last day before the first is refused in the field with the site's words), branch, course and teacher; churn rate, how many left, lost revenue a month and the average lifetime; **the leavers** as bars, a day each for up to 62 days and added up by month for a longer period (a phone has no room for 300 bars; the site draws every day), a press on a bar writing its date and count; the reasons; a **Breakdown** by course, teacher, branch, status, reason or "joined this month" (a field with a list in place of the site's six tabs); the moves between groups with how many left after one and why; with and without a discount; and **Who left** with its own filters (group, reason, discount): a card per student with the day, the group, course and teacher, the reason (amber when none was given), the discount, who removed them and the note. **Set up reasons** (`settings.catalog`) opens the site's dialog as a sheet: each reason with its kind, a tick that switches it on or off, a bin that removes it, and a new reason by name and kind (Leaving or Transfer). **Lead statements** (`reports.leads`): the month's new leads, became students, lost, top source, trials booked, came to trial and top salesperson; the funnel; the year by months as three bars a month (created, converted, lost; the third chart colour, ochre, was checked with the other two for colour-blind readers in both looks); by course and by source; and the trials of each source (new leads, trials, came, became students). One source can be chosen. **Referral programme** (`reports.leads`): leads from invites, friends who joined, coins and bonuses; the year's invites by month; who invited (leads, joined, coins, bonus) and who was invited (by whom, when, joined a group or still a lead). **Students** (`reports.view`): the month, and From and To that start as the month's days and go back to them when the month changes; students, new in the period, in two or more courses, attendance and the average grade (the site's sixth card, "App usage: no student app", is left out: it is not a figure); filters by group, teacher and status (not removed at first); **Attendance report**: expected, present, absent and unmarked, and a card per group that opens the group for someone with `groups.view`; **Performance**: a card per student with the average, courses, teachers and the grade in each group, ten at a time with **Previous page** and **Next page**, a card opening the student. **Center statistics** (`reports.view`): **Monthly**, **Weekly** or **Daily** (a week or a day is taken from a typed date, today at first); the period and working hours in words; utilisation, free room hours, students, potential revenue, free seats and possible students; and a card per room with its numbers (capacity, room hours, lesson hours, free hours, students, free seats, the three seat-hours, total) and under them each of its groups (the site's table has a row per group and a total row per room). **Update room capacities** (`settings.catalog`) opens the app's Rooms. **On the server** one read-only call was added for the app: `GET /api/v1/reports/churn/options?branchId` (`reports.view`) answers the courses, teachers and groups the Left students filters choose from, which the site's page reads on the server itself (the page now reads them through the same service). Until the server has it, the app shows that report without those three filters and asks once. **A fix on the site, found while building this:** `PATCH /api/v1/leave-reasons/:id` read its body with the create form's rules made optional, and those rules fill in what was not sent (kind "Leaving", active). So the switch of a reason, which sends only on or off, turned a Transfer reason into a Leaving one, or was refused when a Leaving reason of that name existed. The change now has rules of its own that keep what was not sent (`leaveReasonUpdateSchema`), with a test. The site's other forms send every field when they change something, so they were not affected. A product's picture is chosen from the phone's photos, cropped square and sent small (the server takes up to 2 MB); a refusal is said under the picture. **Purchase requests**: a status filter and a card per request with the student, product, coins, day, status and who decided; with `coins.manage`, **Approve** and **Reject** on a waiting request (a refusal, such as not enough coins or nothing in stock, is said above the list, which the site does not show), and **New request**: a student found by name or phone with the balance beside each, and a product from those that are active and in stock; a product the student cannot afford is refused in the field. **Shared:** `Tabs` in the reports' parts (a row of tabs that keeps each name's width and scrolls sideways), `TimeField` tells its form what is typed (to tell an empty time from a half-typed one), and `choosePhoto` takes `smallSquare`. On a phone the Family and sign-in cards come after the sections so the groups stay near the top; on a tablet they sit under the person, as on the site. **Not in this part** (part 6b): the group cards with the lesson calendar, split fees, move to another group, back to leads and remove from a group, and the money (refunds, balance corrections, the payments of the old system). **Checked**: 22 new app tests (544 in 47 suites), the app's type check and lint, and the browser build at phone and tablet width, light and dark, against the local server, where every save was answered (extra information, a parent refused for a short phone then added, SMS to the parents and the student, a sibling linked, the family edited, the parents' page texted and replaced, a call started, the removals). The sheet now has four stages: closed, open, sliding and hiding. While a sheet is sliding or hiding it is counted as leaving; a sheet asked for meanwhile waits until the count is zero. After the slide the window is hidden and the sheet waits for iOS to say it is gone (`onDismiss`), or 250 ms if that word does not come. A sheet inside an open sheet (a `Select` in a form) is over that sheet and does not wait. A sheet asked for again while it slides away comes back at once. Android stacks its windows and is left as it was: nothing is counted there. In tests the window is played with `onDismiss` as on an iPhone (`mobile/jest.setup.js`), so a test that picks from a second list right after the first waits for it with `findByTestId`. `sheet.test.tsx` covers a form from a menu and back, and the come-back. The site turns that into "This student is already in the group."; the app showed it on the search field, which is gone once a student is picked, so nothing was said. `isTaken(error, field)` in `mobile/src/lib/form.ts` now recognises the refusal, and the group's add sheet says it under the picked student (`member-picked-problem`), the sheet on a student's page under the group, and the move sheet under the group to move to. Choosing someone else takes the line away. The rule itself is not changed: it is the money rule of the site, and a lead who comes back through **Add to group** on the leads board is taken back into the old place by the server. Whether the office should be able to take a student back from the group's page is kai's to say. **A group's page on a phone.** For someone who may change groups, the page links start with **Manage students** (`open-members`) and the card with what the group is comes before the month of lessons; before, both stood under the whole month. A teacher, who comes to mark lessons, still gets the month first, and a tablet shows both columns as before. **One of something.** `sms.send.recipients`, `groups.members.activated` and `students.activated` in English are plurals now ("1 recipient", "1 student activated"); Russian and Uzbek were already written so that the number fits. This changes the same three sentences on the site with the next server update. **Left as they are, the site does the same:** the timetable shows a typical week from the groups' schedules and has no week to change; a second lead with the same phone is accepted without a warning; the Refund button shows only when the centre has refunds switched on. The app uses `/tests`, `/tests/options`, `/tests/:id`, `/tests/:id/status`, `/tests/:id/attempts`, `/question-bank` and `/question-bank/options` as the site does. The site fix is a site change and arrives with the next server update. | A-251 | **Every site feature in the app, part 6c, step 5c: the import from the old CRM (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** The site's Settings → Import from SOFF CRM (A-143, A-189), the last settings section the app did not have. **The page** keeps the site's order: what the import is, the four files in their order (staff, groups, students, student payments) with where each comes from, then the branch (only for someone with more than one), the file, what the server makes of it, the preview and the result, and the two buttons. **The file** comes from the device's own file picker (`chooseSheet` in `mobile/src/features/files/pick.ts`): an .xlsx or .csv file of up to 5 MB, the server's own limits, checked before anything is sent so a wrong file costs no upload. The name's ending decides the kind, as on the server; a file without an ending is known by its type. On Android every file can be picked and the check says no to the rest, because a file manager there does not always know a .csv by its type and would grey it out. The export has to be on the device first, and the page says so. **What the server says of a file** shows as on the site: which export it is and how many rows, then each column of the file with the Kampus field it goes into and an example from the first rows (a list, not a table, so it reads on a phone), and the columns nothing uses. (2) On the site a preview made for one branch stayed when the branch was changed, so the file could be imported into a branch it was never previewed for; changing the branch now clears the preview. `tests/e2e/soff-import.spec.ts` covers both. **Server:** no new call, no migration, no setting; the app sends the same form to `POST /api/v1/imports/soff` as the site, and the service checks the permission of the matching importer as before. **Not changed:** who may import (the section shows to someone with `students.create`), the 5 MB limit, what each file writes. | A-252 | **Every site feature in the app, part 6d, step 1: the manual with its videos (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** The site's Help with its pictures and videos (A-188, A-199): the Help home, an article and the how-to videos page. **Where the manual comes from.** The site renders the manual from files of its own project (`src/features/help`: the structure once, the words per language, about half a megabyte in all). The app is a project of its own and does not carry a copy that could fall behind: the server answers the manual as data. `GET /api/v1/help?locale=` gives every article the reader may open, whole, in one language (about 140 KB in English and Uzbek, 240 KB in Russian, before the connection packs it): the articles in the site's order, each section's text blocks, its video where this server has the file in that language, and its pictures with their own width and height. `GET /api/v1/help/search?locale=&q=` runs the site's own search (`searchHelp`) on the server, so the app and the site find the same sections in the same order. Both are for any signed-in member of staff, change nothing, and follow the site's one rule about who reads what: the article about Organisations is for the site owner only. A language that is none of the three is answered in Uzbek. The app asks for the manual once and keeps it for the day. **Picture sizes.** Most pictures are a 1280 by 800 page of the site, but some are a single card or a phone's screen. A browser learns a picture's size by loading it; the app has to keep room for a picture before it arrives or the article jumps under the reader's thumb. So the server reads each picture's size from the file's own header (`src/server/help-pictures.ts`, once per file) and says it with the picture. **The Help home** keeps the site's order: the title, the search, "Who are you?" with the reader's own role chosen first (the server says which, by the site's rule) and **All articles**, that role's "start here" lines, the way to the videos with how many there are (only when the server has any), and the articles with what each is about and how many sections it has, two to a row on a tablet. The search answers from two letters once the typing rests; a result shows the article, the section and the sentence found, and opens the article at that section. **An article** shows its title, what it is about, who it is written for, **Open the page**, then "On this page" and the sections in order: the video, the first picture, the text (paragraphs, numbered steps, notes set apart, the names of buttons marked as on the site), further pictures, and at the end the articles before and after it. Differences from the site, each for the phone: "On this page" shows on a phone too (the site shows it only on a wide screen), because an article is long under a thumb; a press on a picture opens it in the app's file page, where two fingers enlarge it, because a whole page of the site is too small to read at a phone's width; a picture taller than 460 points is held to that height; the next or previous article takes the place of the one open, so Back still goes to Help. **Open the page** opens the page inside the app where the app has it and on the site, already signed in, where it does not (it then carries the arrow that says so). **The videos page** lists every video the server has in the app's language in the manual's order, each with **Read the steps**, which opens its article at the section. As on the site nothing of a film is fetched until it is pressed; the player has the device's own controls with full screen and is twice as wide as tall, the shape the site's films are recorded in. **What the manual says is the site's.** The words, pictures and films describe and show the site: a side menu, a header, a mouse. The app has the same pages with the same names, so the steps hold; a manual written and pictured for the app itself would be a second manual to keep in three languages and is not built. The student's article is in the list as on the site; the student's own part of the app has no Help page yet. **In the app's code:** `Screen` can now be asked to bring a place on its page under the header (`scrollRef`), and goes there again if the header turns out taller a moment later, until the reader moves the page; `nativeRoute` knows `/help`, `/help/videos` and `/help/<article>`, so a link to the manual from anywhere opens in the app. `mobile/scripts/serve-web.mjs` (the local server of the browser build) passes the manual's pictures through to the site. **Server:** two new read-only calls, no migration, no setting. Until the server is updated the app's Help page shows an error with **Try again** in place of the manual. **Not changed:** the site's Help pages, the manual's words, who may read which article. Checked in the browser build against the local server on phone and tablet sizes, light and dark: the home by role, the search and opening a result at its section, an article with its pictures at their own shapes, a picture enlarged, a film played (two short test films put on the local server for it), the next article, Open the page, the videos page and an article that does not exist. The plain lines open with the site's signs. A model's conclusion can be written again with the button beside its title. Each figure keeps the site's icon, colour and lines under it (who, which group, how much, how many missed, "and N more"); a figure or a line that points at a page opens that page inside the app, on the site only where the app does not have it. | A-254 | **Every site feature in the app, leftovers, step 1: a group's discounts and lesson packages (added 2026-11-24, kai: "i want you to add all the features from website to the mobile apps as well").** The site's Discounts tab (A-10) and Packages tab (A-178) of a group's page were the two tabs the app's group page did not have. They are two pages of a group now, `/staff/discounts/<group>` and `/staff/packages/<group>`, in the list of the group's pages. **Who sees what** follows the site: Discounts is there for everyone who sees the group, the Packages page only in a group whose billing is by package. **Give a discount** and **Delete** need the right to give discounts; adding, changing and removing a package need the right to change groups; **Sell a package** needs the right to take payments; nothing is changed in an archived group. **No server change.** The app uses the calls the site's tabs use: `GET` and `POST /api/v1/groups/:id/discounts`, `DELETE /api/v1/discounts/:id`, `GET` and `POST /api/v1/groups/:id/packages`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/groups/:id/packages/:packageId`, `POST /api/v1/groups/:id/packages/sell`. A family's discount carries the **Family** mark and has no button, because it is managed on the student's page; a discount with no months left has none either. The scan screen now takes the text from the Enter itself, and from the latest change when the button is pressed. Because the list of scanned badges sits under the open keyboard on a phone, the newest badge is also said in one line above the code field (the name, or the code, and what the server made of it); a first try put the line under the button, and the second look on the simulator found it under the keyboard as well. The line is there from the start, reading "Nothing scanned yet", and keeps its height: when it first appeared with the first badge it pushed the field under the keyboard, which a third look found. **(2) Time zones showed no offset.** The label "Europe/Berlin (GMT+1)" asked the engine for a short offset, and the phone app's engine answers "GMT" for every zone. `timeZoneLabel` in `src/lib/time-zones.ts` (shared by the site and the app) now works the offset out from the zone's own clock, in the same form the site showed before (GMT+1, GMT+5:30, GMT-3:30, GMT+0), so nothing changes on the site. Two guards came with it: the offset is taken to the whole minute (in the second half of a minute it came out a minute short, which no caller met before because they passed whole minutes), and a clock answered in 12-hour form is read with its AM or PM. **(3) On Leads the Owner filter was squashed to a dot.** The Archive tick box beside it took the whole row on a phone and a tablet, because its words were told to fill what room there is; the filter kept only its padding and looked like a stray circle. A tick box has an `inline` form now, as wide as its words, used there. **(4) Small things.** On a tablet's Today the room of a lesson was cut to one letter when the lesson was an extra one: the **Extra** badge now sits with the card's other badges under the group's name, in the row that wraps, so the first line is the time and the room alone (letting the first line wrap did not help on the iPad: it stayed one line). "1 items" under an exercise is "1 item" (the site's message, so the site says it too, with the Russian forms). The card at the end of More said that payments, leads, reports, settings and writing tests are on the site; it now names what really is only there (the organisations page, printing, recording a video lesson), and the empty Today or Checking of an account with nothing to teach points to More instead of the site. In Move and Remove the field for a reason in one's own words is labelled so, not with the choice's words "Other (type below)" a second time. **Left as it is, with the reason.** The simulator has no camera, so after Allow the preview is black with the frame and Stop camera; a refusal shows the notice and Open settings as built; the camera reading a real badge still needs a real phone. The assistant's Summary and Ask tabs scroll with a long conversation. A group's list of students shows initials where the students list shows a photo, because the site's call for a group's members carries no photo. The assistant's test-mode answer is raw data on the local server only. **OPEN for kai, two rules of the site that the app only shows.** (a) Money and status dates follow the server's day (UTC), which A-186 kept on purpose when it moved lesson lookups to the Tashkent day: between midnight and 05:00 Tashkent a new discount reads "Given" yesterday and an activation is stamped yesterday; on the first night of a month that is the month before. DEFAULT: unchanged until kai says the centre's day should rule there too. (b) A student who joins a group in the middle of a month is listed on every lesson of that month, and their calendar counts the earlier ones as not marked; the site's group page and student page do the same. DEFAULT: unchanged. The repairs were looked at on the same two simulators from the branch before merging (run 17b): five codes sent with Enter at once went out whole on each device, the six zone labels read as written here, the Owner filter is a full pill beside Archive in light and dark, and the labels read as intended in three languages; that look sent the Extra badge and the newest-badge line to the places described above. A third look (run 17c) saw the room in full on both devices and the line above the keyboard. No call, no migration, no setting; the app needs a new build, the site gets the two message changes and the label's new arithmetic with its next update. Tests: `scan.test.tsx` (Enter before the last letter, the line above the field, the Extra badge's place on Today), `leads.test.tsx` (the tick box's width), `topic-content.test.tsx` (one item), `tests/unit/time-zones.test.ts` (offsets in winter and summer, half hours, late in a minute, against the engine's own answer). | A-267 | **A privacy policy, and deleting one's own account (added 2026-11-25, kai: "prepare for deploying to play market").** **What Google asks.** A privacy policy on a public address, named in Play Console and in the app. Where an app lets a person open an account, a way to ask for its deletion inside the app and on a web address that names the app, and the same answers in the Data safety form. Apple asks the same. **Who opens an account in Kampus.** A student or a parent does: the first Telegram code on a number the centre has creates their sign-in (`StudentAccount`). A staff member does not: the centre adds them, or approves their sign-in request. **Decision for students.** The sign-in is the person's own, so they delete it themselves and it is gone at once: `DELETE /student-auth/account` removes the `StudentAccount`, the Telegram links made with it (`StudentTelegramChat`, `TelegramContact`) and its unused codes, signs every device out and writes `student.account.delete` to the action log of each linked student. The button is **Delete my account** on the student's home on the site and in the app, and on the public page when a student is signed in. **What stays, and why.** The centre's record of the student: lessons, attendance, marks, homework, payments. It is the centre's own register of its teaching and its money, the centre answers for it, and a student asks the centre to remove it. The public page says so. A later sign-in with the same number makes a new account. **Decision for staff.** A staff account carries the centre's work (lessons taught, payments taken, the action log), so one person cannot remove it alone. **Delete my account** on My account (site and app) sets `User.deletionRequestedAt`, writes `auth.deletionRequest` and sends the notice `ACCOUNT_DELETION` to everyone with `staff.delete` in the organisation, with a link to Staff; they archive the person there, which ends every sign-in. The person can withdraw the request (`auth.deletionWithdraw`). Asking twice changes nothing. **The pages.** `/privacy` and `/delete-account` under each language, open without a sign-in (`OPEN_PAGES` in `src/proxy.ts`), with the wordmark and links to the other two languages. The policy says who answers for the data (the learning centre; Kampus works for it), what is kept, why, what the app asks the device for (camera, microphone, screen, files, notifications), who else handles data (hosting, Telegram, the SMS sender, Payme and Click, Anthropic for the staff assistant, nobody for advertising), how long it is kept, how to see, correct and delete it, and that under-age pupils are signed up by the centre with a parent. **The contact address.** Both pages name `LEGAL_CONTACT_EMAIL` when the server has it; without it they send the reader to their learning centre. **Not done.** Removing a student's whole record on the student's own word (the centre decides); a queue page for staff requests (the notice and the Staff page are enough for the few there will be). **OPEN (kai).** Which e-mail address to publish. The text is Claude's draft from what the code does: kai should read it, and a lawyer should look at where the data is stored against Uzbekistan's personal data law. **Checks.** Unit tests of both services (a student's deletion removes the sign-in and keeps the student; a staff request reaches only those who may archive, once); browser tests of the two public pages, of a staff member asking and withdrawing, and of a student deleting their account at the end of the student sign-in test; the app's screen tests for both buttons. Manual in three languages: one paragraph for staff and one for students. One migration (a column and a notice kind). | A-268 | **Ready for Google Play (added 2026-11-25, kai: "prepare for deploying to play market").** **What Google asks of the file.** An Android App Bundle signed with an upload key; target Android 16 (API 36) since 31 August 2026, which the app already had; native libraries aligned for 16 KB memory pages. **Signing.** `mobile/plugins/with-release-signing.js` adds an `upload` signing config to the generated project. The release is signed with it when the build has `KAMPUS_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE` and `KAMPUS_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD`; without them it keeps the template's test key, so the everyday test file and every existing job build as before. Google keeps the app's final key (Play App Signing), so a lost upload key can be replaced. **The key is kai's.** `mobile/scripts/play-upload-key.sh` is run by kai on the Mac, once: a random password goes into the Mac's Keychain, the key file to `~/Desktop/Private/`, both into the repository's GitHub secrets, and only the certificate's fingerprint is printed. Claude does not run it, and never reads the file, the Keychain item or the secrets. **The build.** The workflow **Google Play bundle** (`.github/workflows/mobile-play.yml`), started by hand, builds `bundleRelease` for every processor kind against `https://kampus.center`, refuses a manifest that allows plain http, checks that the bundle is signed with the given key and that its 64-bit libraries are aligned to 16 KB, and keeps `kampus-play-<number>.aab` for 30 days. The build number is the run's number, so each upload is higher than the last. On a pull request that touches the build it runs the same steps with a key made up for the run, so the path is proven before kai's key exists. **16 KB.** `mobile/scripts/check-page-size.sh` reads every `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64` library's load alignment; it now also runs on the everyday test file. All 62 libraries of the current build pass, and `zipalign -c -P 16` agrees on the Mac. **The store page.** `mobile/store/listing.json` has the name, the short and the full description in English, Russian and Uzbek, held to Google's lengths by a test; `icon-512.png` and `feature.png` are drawn by `make-graphics.cjs` from the app's icon and the sign-in page's tile wall. 26 screenshots from the Android emulators (seed data, made-up people) are on the Mac in `~/Desktop/kampus-play/screenshots/`: six phone pictures per language, four for 7-inch and four for 10-inch tablets, cut to the 2:1 limit Google sets. **kai's part** is in [PLAY-STORE.md](PLAY-STORE.md): the Play Console account, the contact address, the key, the server update, the forms (with Claude's answers for Data safety, content rating, audience and the screen-share service), sign-ins for Google's reviewers, the test tracks. **Repair on the way.** `Check` with `inline` on Android cut its label's last letter (Uzbek **Arxiv** read "Arxi" on Leads): the label no longer shrinks. **Not done.** Uploading to Play by itself (needs a service account from kai's Play Console); push notifications (Firebase); the App Store. **Checks.** A test of the signing plugin on the template's own build file; a test of the listing's lengths; the page-size and signature scripts run on a real bundle in the workflow; the key script run in the cloud with stand-ins for `gh` and the Keychain.
